462.text: And they kept calling out to Lot and saying to him: “Where are the men who came in to you tonight? Bring them out to us that we may have intercourse with them.”

463.label: Genesis 19:6
463.text: Finally Lot went out to them to the entrance, but he shut the door behind him.

464.label: Genesis 19:7
464.text: Then he said: “Please, my brothers, do not act badly.

465.label: Genesis 19:8
465.text: Please, here I have two daughters who have never had intercourse with a man. Please, let me bring them out to YOU. Then do to them as is good in YOUR eyes. Only to these men do not do a thing, because that is why they have come under the shadow of my roof.”

466.label: Genesis 19:9
466.text: At this they said: “Stand back there!” And they added: “This lone man came here to reside as an alien and yet he would actually play the judge. Now we are going to do worse to you than to them.” And they came pressing heavily in on the man, on Lot, and were getting near to break in the door.

467.label: Genesis 19:10
467.text: So the men thrust out their hands and brought Lot in to them, into the house, and they shut the door.

468.label: Genesis 19:11
468.text: But they struck with blindness the men who were at the entrance of the house, from the least to the greatest, so that they were wearing themselves out trying to find the entrance.

469.label: Genesis 19:12
469.text: Then the men said to Lot: “Do you have anyone else here? Son-in-law and your sons and your daughters and all who are yours in the city, bring out of the place!

470.label: Genesis 19:13
470.text: For we are bringing this place to ruin, because the outcry against them has grown loud before Jehovah, so that Jehovah sent us to bring the city to ruin.”

471.label: Genesis 19:14
471.text: Hence Lot went on out and began to speak to his sons-in-law who were to take his daughters, and he kept on saying: “Get up! Get out of this place, because Jehovah is bringing the city to ruin!” But in the eyes of his sons-in-law he seemed like a man who was joking.

472.label: Genesis 19:15
472.text: However, when the dawn ascended, then the angels became urgent with Lot, saying: “Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are found here, for fear you may be swept away in the error of the city!”

473.label: Genesis 19:16
473.text: When he kept lingering, then in the compassion of Jehovah upon him, the men seized hold of his hand and of the hand of his wife and of the hands of his two daughters and they proceeded to bring him out and to station him outside the city.

474.label: Genesis 19:17
474.text: And it came about that, as soon as they had brought them forth to the outskirts, he began to say: “Escape for your soul! Do not look behind you and do not stand still in all the District! Escape to the mountainous region for fear you may be swept away!”

475.label: Genesis 19:18
475.text: Then Lot said to them: “Not that, please, Jehovah!

476.label: Genesis 19:19
476.text: Please, now, your servant has found favor in your eyes so that you are magnifying your loving-kindness, which you have exercised with me to preserve my soul alive, but I—I am not able to escape to the mountainous region for fear calamity may keep close to me and I certainly die.

477.label: Genesis 19:20
477.text: Please, now, this city is nearby to flee there and it is a small thing. May I, please, escape there—is it not a small thing?—and my soul will live on.”

478.label: Genesis 19:21
478.text: So he said to him: “Here I do show you consideration to this extent also, by my not overthrowing the city of which you have spoken.

479.label: Genesis 19:22
479.text: Hurry! Escape there, because I am not able to do a thing until your arriving there!” That is why he called the name of the city Zoʹar.

480.label: Genesis 19:23
480.text: The sun had gone forth over the land when Lot arrived at Zoʹar.

481.label: Genesis 19:24
481.text: Then Jehovah made it rain sulphur and fire from Jehovah, from the heavens, upon Sodʹom and upon Go·morʹrah.

482.label: Genesis 19:25
482.text: So he went ahead overthrowing these cities, even the entire District and all the inhabitants of the cities and the plants of the ground.

483.label: Genesis 19:26
483.text: And his wife began to look around from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.

484.label: Genesis 19:27
484.text: Now Abraham made his way early in the morning to the place where he had stood before Jehovah.

485.label: Genesis 19:28
485.text: Then he looked down toward Sodʹom and Go·morʹrah and toward all the land of the District and saw a sight. Why, here thick smoke ascended from the land like the thick smoke of a kiln!

486.label: Genesis 19:29
486.text: And it came about that when God brought the cities of the District to ruin God kept Abraham in mind in that he took steps to send Lot out of the midst of the overthrow when overthrowing the cities among which Lot had been dwelling.

487.label: Genesis 19:30
487.text: Later Lot went up from Zoʹar and began dwelling in the mountainous region, and his two daughters along with him, because he got afraid of dwelling in Zoʹar. So he began dwelling in a cave, he and his two daughters.

488.label: Genesis 19:31
488.text: And the firstborn proceeded to say to the younger woman: “Our father is old and there is not a man in the land to have relations with us according to the way of the whole earth.

489.label: Genesis 19:32
489.text: Come, let us give our father wine to drink and let us lie down with him and preserve offspring from our father.”

490.label: Genesis 19:33
490.text: So they kept giving their father wine to drink during that night; then the firstborn went in and lay down with her father, but he did not know when she lay down and when she got up.

491.label: Genesis 19:34
491.text: And it came about on the next day that the firstborn then said to the younger: “Here I lay down with my father last night. Let us give him wine to drink tonight also. Then you go in, lie down with him, and let us preserve offspring from our father.”

492.label: Genesis 19:35
492.text: So they repeatedly gave their father wine to drink during that night also; then the younger got up and lay down with him, but he did not know when she lay down and when she got up.

493.label: Genesis 19:36
493.text: And both the daughters of Lot became pregnant from their father.

494.label: Genesis 19:37
494.text: In time the firstborn became mother to a son and called his name Moʹab. He is the father of Moʹab, to this day.

495.label: Genesis 19:38
495.text: As for the younger, she too gave birth to a son and then called his name Ben-amʹmi. He is the father of the sons of Amʹmon, to this day.

496.label: Genesis 20:1
496.text: Now Abraham moved camp from there to the land of the Negʹeb and took up dwelling between Kaʹdesh and Shur and residing as an alien at Geʹrar.

497.label: Genesis 20:2
497.text: And Abraham repeated concerning Sarah his wife: “She is my sister.” With that A·bimʹe·lech king of Geʹrar sent and took Sarah.

498.label: Genesis 20:3
498.text: Afterward God came to A·bimʹe·lech in a dream by night and said to him: “Here you are as good as dead because of the woman whom you have taken, since she is owned by another owner as his wife.”

499.label: Genesis 20:4
499.text: However, A·bimʹe·lech had not gone near her. Hence he said: “Jehovah, will you kill a nation that is really righteous?

500.label: Genesis 20:5
500.text: Did not he say to me, ‘She is my sister’? and she—did not she too say, ‘He is my brother’? In the honesty of my heart and with innocency of my hands I have done this.”

501.label: Genesis 20:6
501.text: At that the [true] God said to him in the dream: “I too have known that in the honesty of your heart you have done this, and I was also holding you back from sinning against me. That is why I did not allow you to touch her.

502.label: Genesis 20:7
502.text: But now return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet, and he will make supplication for you. So keep living. But if you are not returning her, know that you will positively die, you and all who are yours.”

503.label: Genesis 20:8
503.text: So A·bimʹe·lech got up early in the morning and proceeded to call all his servants and to speak of all these things in their ears. And the men got very much afraid.

504.label: Genesis 20:9
504.text: Then A·bimʹe·lech called Abraham and said to him: “What have you done to us, and what sin have I committed against you, in that you have brought upon me and my kingdom a great sin? Deeds that should not have been done you have done in connection with me.”

505.label: Genesis 20:10
505.text: And A·bimʹe·lech went on to say to Abraham: “What did you have in view in that you have done this thing?”

506.label: Genesis 20:11
506.text: To this Abraham said: “It was because I said to myself, ‘Doubtless there is no fear of God in this place, and they will certainly kill me because of my wife.’

507.label: Genesis 20:12
507.text: And, besides, she is truly my sister, the daughter of my father, only not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife.

508.label: Genesis 20:13
508.text: And it came about that, when God caused me to wander from the house of my father, then I said to her, ‘This is your loving-kindness which you may exercise toward me: At every place where we shall come say of me: “He is my brother.”’”

509.label: Genesis 20:14
509.text: Following that A·bimʹe·lech took sheep and cattle and menservants and maidservants and gave them to Abraham and returned to him Sarah his wife.

510.label: Genesis 20:15
510.text: Further A·bimʹe·lech said: “Here my land is available to you. Dwell where it is good in your eyes.”

511.label: Genesis 20:16
511.text: And to Sarah he said: “Here I do give a thousand silver pieces of money to your brother. Here it is for you a covering of the eyes to all who are with you, and before everybody, and you are cleared of reproach.”

512.label: Genesis 20:17
512.text: And Abraham began to make supplication to the [true] God; and God proceeded to heal A·bimʹe·lech and his wife and his slave girls, and they began bearing children.

513.label: Genesis 20:18
513.text: For Jehovah had tightly shut up every womb of the house of A·bimʹe·lech because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.

514.label: Genesis 21:1
514.text: And Jehovah turned his attention to Sarah just as he had said, and Jehovah now did to Sarah just as he had spoken.

515.label: Genesis 21:2
515.text: And Sarah became pregnant and then bore a son to Abraham in his old age at the appointed time of which God had spoken to him.

516.label: Genesis 21:3
516.text: Accordingly Abraham called the name of his son who had been born to him, whom Sarah had borne to him, Isaac.

517.label: Genesis 21:4
517.text: And Abraham proceeded to circumcise Isaac his son when eight days old, just as God had commanded him.

518.label: Genesis 21:5
518.text: And Abraham was a hundred years old when Isaac his son was born to him.

519.label: Genesis 21:6
519.text: Then Sarah said: “God has prepared laughter for me: everybody hearing of it will laugh at me.”

520.label: Genesis 21:7
520.text: And she added: “Who would have uttered to Abraham, ‘Sarah will certainly suckle children,’ whereas I have given birth to a son in his old age?”

521.label: Genesis 21:8
521.text: Now the child kept growing and came to be weaned; and Abraham then prepared a big feast on the day of Isaac’s being weaned.

522.label: Genesis 21:9
522.text: And Sarah kept noticing the son of Haʹgar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, poking fun.

523.label: Genesis 21:10
523.text: So she began to say to Abraham: “Drive out this slave girl and her son, for the son of this slave girl is not going to be an heir with my son, with Isaac!”

524.label: Genesis 21:11
524.text: But the thing proved to be very displeasing to Abraham as regards his son.

525.label: Genesis 21:12
525.text: Then God said to Abraham: “Do not let anything that Sarah keeps saying to you be displeasing to you about the boy and about your slave girl. Listen to her voice, because it is by means of Isaac that what will be called your seed will be.

526.label: Genesis 21:13
526.text: And as for the son of the slave girl, I shall also constitute him a nation, because he is your offspring.”

527.label: Genesis 21:14
527.text: So Abraham got up early in the morning and took bread and a skin water bottle and gave it to Haʹgar, setting it upon her shoulder, and the child, and then dismissed her. And she went her way and wandered about in the wilderness of Beʹer-sheʹba.

528.label: Genesis 21:15
528.text: Finally the water became exhausted in the skin bottle and she threw the child under one of the bushes.

529.label: Genesis 21:16
529.text: Then she went on and sat down by herself, about the distance of a bowshot away, because she said: “Let me not see it when the child dies.” So she sat down at a distance and began to raise her voice and weep.

530.label: Genesis 21:17
530.text: At that God heard the voice of the boy, and God’s angel called to Haʹgar out of the heavens and said to her: “What is the matter with you, Haʹgar? Do not be afraid, because God has listened to the voice of the boy there where he is.

531.label: Genesis 21:18
531.text: Get up, lift up the boy and take hold of him with your hand, because I shall constitute him a great nation.”

532.label: Genesis 21:19
532.text: Then God opened her eyes so that she caught sight of a well of water; and she went and began to fill the skin bottle with water and to give the boy a drink.

533.label: Genesis 21:20
533.text: And God continued to be with the boy, and he kept growing and dwelling in the wilderness; and he became an archer.

534.label: Genesis 21:21
534.text: And he took up dwelling in the wilderness of Paʹran, and his mother proceeded to take a wife for him from the land of Egypt.

535.label: Genesis 21:22
535.text: Now it came about at that time that A·bimʹe·lech together with Phiʹcol the chief of his army said to Abraham: “God is with you in everything you are doing.

536.label: Genesis 21:23
536.text: So now swear to me here by God that you will not prove false to me and to my offspring and to my posterity; that, according to the loyal love with which I have dealt with you, you will deal with me and with the land in which you have been residing as an alien.”

538.label: Genesis 21:25
538.text: When Abraham criticized A·bimʹe·lech severely as regards the well of water that the servants of A·bimʹe·lech had seized by violence,

539.label: Genesis 21:26
539.text: then A·bimʹe·lech said: “I do not know who did this thing, neither did you yourself tell it to me, and I myself have also not heard of it except today.”

540.label: Genesis 21:27
540.text: With that Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to A·bimʹe·lech, and both of them proceeded to conclude a covenant.

541.label: Genesis 21:28
541.text: When Abraham set seven female lambs of the flock by themselves,

542.label: Genesis 21:29
542.text: A·bimʹe·lech went on to say to Abraham: “What is the meaning here of these seven female lambs that you have set by themselves?”

543.label: Genesis 21:30
543.text: Then he said: “You are to accept the seven female lambs at my hand, that it may serve as a witness for me that I have dug this well.”

544.label: Genesis 21:31
544.text: That is why he called that place Beʹer-sheʹba, because there both of them had taken an oath.

545.label: Genesis 21:32
545.text: So they concluded a covenant at Beʹer-sheʹba, after which A·bimʹe·lech got up together with Phiʹcol the chief of his army and they returned to the land of the Phi·lisʹtines.

546.label: Genesis 21:33
546.text: After that he planted a tamarisk tree at Beʹer-sheʹba and called there upon the name of Jehovah the indefinitely lasting God.

547.label: Genesis 21:34
547.text: And Abraham extended his residence as an alien in the land of the Phi·lisʹtines many days.

548.label: Genesis 22:1
548.text: Now after these things it came about that the [true] God put Abraham to the test. Accordingly he said to him: “Abraham!” to which he said: “Here I am!”

549.label: Genesis 22:2
549.text: And he went on to say: “Take, please, your son, your only son whom you so love, Isaac, and make a trip to the land of Mo·riʹah and there offer him up as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I shall designate to you.”

550.label: Genesis 22:3
550.text: So Abraham got up early in the morning and saddled his ass and took two of his attendants with him and Isaac his son; and he split the wood for the burnt offering. Then he rose and went on the trip to the place that the [true] God designated to him.

551.label: Genesis 22:4
551.text: It was first on the third day that Abraham raised his eyes and began to see the place from a distance.

552.label: Genesis 22:5
552.text: Abraham now said to his attendants: “YOU stay here with the ass, but I and the boy want to go on over there and worship and return to YOU.”

553.label: Genesis 22:6
553.text: After that Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and put it upon Isaac his son and took in his hands the fire and the slaughtering knife, and both of them went on together.

554.label: Genesis 22:7
554.text: And Isaac began to say to Abraham his father: “My father!” In turn he said: “Here I am, my son!” So he continued: “Here are the fire and the wood, but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?”

555.label: Genesis 22:8
555.text: To this Abraham said: “God will provide himself the sheep for the burnt offering, my son.” And both of them walked on together.

556.label: Genesis 22:9
556.text: Finally they reached the place that the [true] God had designated to him, and Abraham built an altar there and set the wood in order and bound Isaac his son hand and foot and put him upon the altar on top of the wood.

557.label: Genesis 22:10
557.text: Then Abraham put out his hand and took the slaughtering knife to kill his son.

558.label: Genesis 22:11
558.text: But Jehovah’s angel began calling to him out of the heavens and saying: “Abraham, Abraham!” to which he answered: “Here I am!”

559.label: Genesis 22:12
559.text: And he went on to say: “Do not put out your hand against the boy and do not do anything at all to him, for now I do know that you are God-fearing in that you have not withheld your son, your only one, from me.”

560.label: Genesis 22:13
560.text: At that Abraham raised his eyes and looked and there, deep in the foreground, there was a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. So Abraham went and took the ram and offered it up for a burnt offering in place of his son.

561.label: Genesis 22:14
561.text: And Abraham began to call the name of that place Je·hoʹvah-jiʹreh. This is why it is customarily said today: “In the mountain of Jehovah it will be provided.”

562.label: Genesis 22:15
562.text: And Jehovah’s angel proceeded to call to Abraham the second time out of the heavens

563.label: Genesis 22:16
563.text: and to say: “‘By myself I do swear,’ is the utterance of Jehovah, ‘that by reason of the fact that you have done this thing and you have not withheld your son, your only one,

564.label: Genesis 22:17
564.text: I shall surely bless you and I shall surely multiply your seed like the stars of the heavens and like the grains of sand that are on the seashore; and your seed will take possession of the gate of his enemies.

565.label: Genesis 22:18
565.text: And by means of your seed all nations of the earth will certainly bless themselves due to the fact that you have listened to my voice.’”

566.label: Genesis 22:19
566.text: After that Abraham returned to his attendants, and they got up and went their way together to Beʹer-sheʹba; and Abraham continued to dwell at Beʹer-sheʹba.

567.label: Genesis 22:20
567.text: Now it came about after these things that the report got through to Abraham: “Here Milʹcah herself has also borne sons to Naʹhor your brother:

568.label: Genesis 22:21
568.text: Uz his firstborn and Buz his brother and Kem·uʹel the father of Aʹram,

569.label: Genesis 22:22
569.text: and Cheʹsed and Haʹzo and Pilʹdash and Jidʹlaph and Be·thuʹel.”

570.label: Genesis 22:23
570.text: And Be·thuʹel became the father of Re·bekʹah. These eight Milʹcah bore to Naʹhor the brother of Abraham.

571.label: Genesis 22:24
571.text: There was his concubine too, whose name was Reuʹmah. In time she herself also gave birth to Teʹbah and Gaʹham and Taʹhash and Maʹa·cah.

572.label: Genesis 23:1
572.text: And Sarah’s life got to be a hundred and twenty-seven years long. They were the years of Sarah’s life.

573.label: Genesis 23:2
573.text: So Sarah died in Kirʹi·ath-arʹba, that is to say, Heʹbron, in the land of Caʹnaan, and Abraham came in to bewail Sarah and to weep over her.

574.label: Genesis 23:3
574.text: Then Abraham got up from before his dead and proceeded to speak to the sons of Heth, saying:

575.label: Genesis 23:4
575.text: “An alien resident and settler I am among YOU. Give me the possession of a burial place among YOU that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”

576.label: Genesis 23:5
576.text: At this the sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him:

577.label: Genesis 23:6
577.text: “Hear us, my lord. A chieftain of God you are in the midst of us. In the choicest of our burial places bury your dead. None of us will hold back his burial place from you to prevent burying your dead.”

578.label: Genesis 23:7
578.text: Thereupon Abraham got up and bowed down to the natives, to the sons of Heth,

579.label: Genesis 23:8
579.text: and spoke with them, saying: “If YOUR souls agree to bury my dead out of my sight, listen to me and urge Eʹphron the son of Zoʹhar for me,

580.label: Genesis 23:9
580.text: that he may give me the cave of Mach·peʹlah, which is his, which is at the extremity of his field. For the full amount of silver let him give it to me in the midst of YOU for the possession of a burial place.”

581.label: Genesis 23:10
581.text: As it was, Eʹphron was sitting among the sons of Heth. So Eʹphron the Hitʹtite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Heth with all those entering the gate of his city, saying:

582.label: Genesis 23:11
582.text: “No, my lord! Listen to me. The field I do give to you, and the cave that is in it to you I do give it. Before the eyes of the sons of my people I do give it to you. Bury your dead.”

583.label: Genesis 23:12
583.text: At that Abraham bowed down before the natives

584.label: Genesis 23:13
584.text: and spoke to Eʹphron in the hearing of the natives, saying: “Only if you—no, listen to me! I will give you the amount of silver for the field. Take it from me, that I may bury my dead there.”

585.label: Genesis 23:14
585.text: Then Eʹphron answered Abraham, saying to him:

586.label: Genesis 23:15
586.text: “My lord, listen to me. A land plot worth four hundred silver shekels, what is that between me and you? So bury your dead.”

587.label: Genesis 23:16
587.text: Accordingly Abraham listened to Eʹphron, and Abraham weighed out to Eʹphron the amount of silver that he had spoken in the hearing of the sons of Heth, four hundred silver shekels current with the merchants.

588.label: Genesis 23:17
588.text: Thus the field of Eʹphron that was in Mach·peʹlah, which is in front of Mamʹre, the field and the cave that was in it and all the trees that were in the field, which were within all its boundaries round about, became confirmed

589.label: Genesis 23:18
589.text: to Abraham as his purchased property before the eyes of the sons of Heth among all those entering the gate of his city.

590.label: Genesis 23:19
590.text: And after that Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Mach·peʹlah in front of Mamʹre, that is to say, Heʹbron, in the land of Caʹnaan.

591.label: Genesis 23:20
591.text: Thus the field and the cave that was in it became confirmed to Abraham for the possession of a burial place at the hands of the sons of Heth.

592.label: Genesis 24:1
592.text: Now Abraham was old, advanced in years; and Jehovah had blessed Abraham in everything.

593.label: Genesis 24:2
593.text: Hence Abraham said to his servant, the oldest one of his household, who was managing all he had: “Put your hand, please, under my thigh,

594.label: Genesis 24:3
594.text: as I must have you swear by Jehovah, the God of the heavens and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Caʹnaan·ites in among whom I am dwelling,

595.label: Genesis 24:4
595.text: but you will go to my country and to my relatives, and you will certainly take a wife for my son, for Isaac.”

596.label: Genesis 24:5
596.text: However, the servant said to him: “What if the woman does not wish to come with me to this land? Must I be sure to return your son to the land from where you went out?”

597.label: Genesis 24:6
597.text: At this Abraham said to him: “Be on your guard that you do not return my son there.

598.label: Genesis 24:7
598.text: Jehovah the God of the heavens, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my relatives and who spoke to me and who swore to me, saying, ‘To your seed I am going to give this land,’ he will send his angel ahead of you, and you will certainly take a wife for my son from there.

599.label: Genesis 24:8
599.text: But if the woman should not wish to come with you, you also will have become free from this oath you gave me. Only you must not return my son there.”

600.label: Genesis 24:9
600.text: With that the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter.

601.label: Genesis 24:10
601.text: So the servant took ten camels from the camels of his master and proceeded to go with every sort of good thing of his master’s in his hand. Then he rose and got on his way to Mes·o·po·taʹmi·a to the city of Naʹhor.

602.label: Genesis 24:11
602.text: Eventually he had the camels kneel down outside the city at a well of water about evening time, about the time that the women who draw water were accustomed to go out.

603.label: Genesis 24:12
603.text: And he went on to say: “Jehovah the God of my master Abraham, cause it to happen, please, before me this day and perform loving-kindness with my master Abraham.

604.label: Genesis 24:13
604.text: Here I am stationed at a fountain of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

605.label: Genesis 24:14
605.text: What must occur is that the young woman to whom I shall say, ‘Let your water jar down, please, that I may take a drink,’ and who will indeed say, ‘Take a drink, and I shall also water your camels,’ this is the one you must assign to your servant, to Isaac; and by this let me know that you have performed loyal love with my master.”

606.label: Genesis 24:15
606.text: Well, it came about that before he had finished speaking, why, here coming out was Re·bekʹah, who had been born to Be·thuʹel the son of Milʹcah the wife of Naʹhor, Abraham’s brother, and her water jar was upon her shoulder.

607.label: Genesis 24:16
607.text: Now the young woman was very attractive in appearance, a virgin, and no man had had sexual intercourse with her; and she made her way down to the fountain and began to fill her water jar and then came up.

608.label: Genesis 24:17
608.text: At once the servant ran to meet her and said: “Give me, please, a little sip of water from your jar.”

609.label: Genesis 24:18
609.text: In turn she said: “Drink, my lord.” With that she quickly lowered her jar upon her hand and gave him a drink.

610.label: Genesis 24:19
610.text: When she was finished giving him a drink, then she said: “For your camels too I shall draw water until they are done drinking.”

611.label: Genesis 24:20
611.text: So she quickly emptied her jar into the drinking trough and ran yet again and again to the well to draw water, and kept drawing for all his camels.

612.label: Genesis 24:21
612.text: All the while the man was gazing at her in wonder, keeping silent to know whether Jehovah had made his trip successful or not.

613.label: Genesis 24:22
613.text: Consequently it came about that, when the camels had finished drinking, then the man took a gold nose ring of a half shekel in weight and two bracelets for her hands, ten shekels of gold was their weight,

614.label: Genesis 24:23
614.text: and he went on to say: “Whose daughter are you? Tell me, please. Is there any room at the house of your father for us to spend the night?”

615.label: Genesis 24:24
615.text: At that she said to him: “I am the daughter of Be·thuʹel the son of Milʹcah, whom she bore to Naʹhor.”

616.label: Genesis 24:25
616.text: And she said further to him: “There is both straw and much fodder with us, also a place to spend the night.”

617.label: Genesis 24:26
617.text: And the man proceeded to bow down and prostrate himself before Jehovah

618.label: Genesis 24:27
618.text: and say: “Blessed be Jehovah the God of my master Abraham, who has not left his loving-kindness and his trustworthiness toward my master. I being on the way, Jehovah has led me to the house of the brothers of my master.”

619.label: Genesis 24:28
619.text: And the young woman went running and telling the household of her mother about these things.

620.label: Genesis 24:29
620.text: Now Re·bekʹah had a brother and his name was Laʹban. So Laʹban went running to the man who was outside at the fountain.

621.label: Genesis 24:30
621.text: And it came about that on seeing the nose ring and the bracelets on the hands of his sister and on hearing the words of Re·bekʹah his sister, saying: “This is the way the man spoke to me,” then he came to the man and there he was, standing by the camels at the fountain.

622.label: Genesis 24:31
622.text: At once he said: “Come, you blessed one of Jehovah. Why do you keep standing out here, when I myself have made the house ready and room for the camels?”

623.label: Genesis 24:32
623.text: With that the man came on into the house, and he went unharnessing the camels and giving straw and fodder to the camels and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.

624.label: Genesis 24:33
624.text: Then something to eat was set before him, but he said: “I shall not eat until I have spoken about my matters.” Hence he said: “Speak!”

625.label: Genesis 24:34
625.text: Then he went on to say: “I am Abraham’s servant.

626.label: Genesis 24:35
626.text: And Jehovah has blessed my master very much in that he goes on making him greater and giving him sheep and cattle and silver and gold and menservants and maidservants and camels and asses.

627.label: Genesis 24:36
627.text: Further, Sarah the wife of my master bore a son to my master after her growing old; and he will give him everything he has.

628.label: Genesis 24:37
628.text: So my master made me swear, saying, ‘You must not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Caʹnaan·ites in whose land I am dwelling.

629.label: Genesis 24:38
629.text: No, but you will go to the house of my father and to my family and you must take a wife for my son.’

630.label: Genesis 24:39
630.text: But I said to my master, ‘What if the woman will not come with me?’

631.label: Genesis 24:40
631.text: Then he said to me, ‘Jehovah, before whom I have walked, will send his angel with you and will certainly give success to your way; and you must take a wife for my son from my family and from the house of my father.

632.label: Genesis 24:41
632.text: At that time you will be cleared of obligation to me by oath when you get to my family, and if they will not give her to you, then you shall become free of obligation to me by oath.’

633.label: Genesis 24:42
633.text: “When I got to the fountain today, then I said, ‘Jehovah the God of my master Abraham, if you are really giving success to my way on which I am going,

634.label: Genesis 24:43
634.text: here I am stationed at a fountain of water. What must occur is that the maiden coming out to draw water to whom I shall actually say: “Please, let me drink a little water from your jar,”

635.label: Genesis 24:44
635.text: and who will indeed say to me: “Both you take a drink, and I shall also draw water for your camels,” she is the woman whom Jehovah has assigned for the son of my master.’

636.label: Genesis 24:45
636.text: “Before I was finished speaking in my heart, why, there was Re·bekʹah coming out, with her jar upon her shoulder; and she made her way down to the fountain and began to draw water. Then I said to her, ‘Give me a drink, please.’

637.label: Genesis 24:46
637.text: So she quickly lowered her jar from off her and said, ‘Take a drink, and I shall also water your camels.’ Then I took a drink, and she also watered the camels.

638.label: Genesis 24:47
638.text: After that I asked her and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ to which she said, ‘The daughter of Be·thuʹel the son of Naʹhor, whom Milʹcah bore to him.’ Accordingly I put the nose ring on her nostril and the bracelets on her hands.

639.label: Genesis 24:48
639.text: And I proceeded to bow down and prostrate myself before Jehovah and bless Jehovah the God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the true way to take the daughter of the brother of my master for his son.

640.label: Genesis 24:49
640.text: And now if YOU are actually exercising loving-kindness and trustworthiness toward my master, tell me; but if not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand or to the left.”

641.label: Genesis 24:50
641.text: Then Laʹban and Be·thuʹel answered and said: “From Jehovah this thing has issued. We are unable to speak bad or good to you.

642.label: Genesis 24:51
642.text: Here is Re·bekʹah before you. Take her and go, and let her become a wife to the son of your master, just as Jehovah has spoken.”

643.label: Genesis 24:52
643.text: And it came about that when Abraham’s servant had heard their words, he at once prostrated himself on the earth before Jehovah.

644.label: Genesis 24:53
644.text: And the servant began to bring out articles of silver and articles of gold and garments and to give them to Re·bekʹah; and he gave choice things to her brother and to her mother.

645.label: Genesis 24:54
645.text: After that they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and they spent the night there and got up in the morning. Then he said: “SEND me off to my master.”

646.label: Genesis 24:55
646.text: To this her brother and her mother said: “Let the young woman stay with us at least ten days. Afterward she can go.”

647.label: Genesis 24:56
647.text: But he said to them: “Do not detain me, seeing that Jehovah has given success to my way. Send me off, that I may go to my master.”

648.label: Genesis 24:57
648.text: So they said: “Let us call the young woman and inquire at her mouth.”

649.label: Genesis 24:58
649.text: Then they called Re·bekʹah and said to her: “Will you go with this man?” In turn she said: “I am willing to go.”

650.label: Genesis 24:59
650.text: At that they sent off Re·bekʹah their sister and her nurse and Abraham’s servant and his men.

651.label: Genesis 24:60
651.text: And they began to bless Re·bekʹah and say to her: “O you, our sister, may you become thousands times ten thousand, and let your seed take possession of the gate of those who hate it.”

652.label: Genesis 24:61
652.text: After that Re·bekʹah and her lady attendants rose and they went riding on the camels and following the man; and the servant took Re·bekʹah and got on his way.

653.label: Genesis 24:62
653.text: Now Isaac had come from the way that goes to Beʹer-laʹhai-roi, for he was dwelling in the land of the Negʹeb.

654.label: Genesis 24:63
654.text: And Isaac was out walking in order to meditate in the field at about the falling of evening. When he raised his eyes and looked, why, there camels were coming!

655.label: Genesis 24:64
655.text: When Re·bekʹah raised her eyes, she caught sight of Isaac and she swung herself down from off the camel.

656.label: Genesis 24:65
656.text: Then she said to the servant: “Who is that man there walking in the field to meet us?” and the servant said: “It is my master.” And she proceeded to take a headcloth and to cover herself.

657.label: Genesis 24:66
657.text: And the servant went relating to Isaac all the things he had done.

658.label: Genesis 24:67
658.text: After that Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother. Thus he took Re·bekʹah and she became his wife; and he fell in love with her, and Isaac found comfort after the loss of his mother.

659.label: Genesis 25:1
659.text: Furthermore, Abraham again took a wife, and her name was Ke·tuʹrah.

660.label: Genesis 25:2
660.text: In time she bore him Zimʹran and Jokʹshan and Meʹdan and Midʹi·an and Ishʹbak and Shuʹah.

661.label: Genesis 25:3
661.text: And Jokʹshan became father to Sheʹba and Deʹdan. And the sons of Deʹdan became As·shuʹrim and Le·tuʹshim and Le·umʹmim.

662.label: Genesis 25:4
662.text: And the sons of Midʹi·an were Eʹphah and Eʹpher and Haʹnoch and A·biʹda and El·daʹah. All these were the sons of Ke·tuʹrah.

663.label: Genesis 25:5
663.text: Later on Abraham gave everything he had to Isaac,

664.label: Genesis 25:6
664.text: but to the sons of the concubines that Abraham had Abraham gave gifts. Then he sent them away from Isaac his son, while he was still alive, eastward, to the land of the East.

665.label: Genesis 25:7
665.text: And these are the days of the years of Abraham’s life which he lived, a hundred and seventy-five years.

666.label: Genesis 25:8
666.text: Then Abraham expired and died in a good old age, old and satisfied, and was gathered to his people.

667.label: Genesis 25:9
667.text: So Isaac and Ishʹma·el his sons buried him in the cave of Mach·peʹlah in the field of Eʹphron the son of Zoʹhar the Hitʹtite that is in front of Mamʹre,

668.label: Genesis 25:10
668.text: the field that Abraham had purchased from the sons of Heth. There Abraham was buried, and also Sarah his wife.

669.label: Genesis 25:11
669.text: And it developed that after Abraham’s death God continued to bless Isaac his son, and Isaac was dwelling close by Beʹer-laʹhai-roi.

670.label: Genesis 25:12
670.text: And this is the history of Ishʹma·el the son of Abraham whom Haʹgar the Egyptian the maidservant of Sarah bore to Abraham.

671.label: Genesis 25:13
671.text: Now these are the names of the sons of Ishʹma·el, by their names, according to their family origins: Ishʹma·el’s firstborn Ne·baʹioth and Keʹdar and Adʹbe·el and Mibʹsam

672.label: Genesis 25:14
672.text: and Mishʹma and Duʹmah and Masʹsa,

673.label: Genesis 25:15
673.text: Haʹdad and Teʹma, Jeʹtur, Naʹphish and Kedʹe·mah.

674.label: Genesis 25:16
674.text: These are the sons of Ishʹma·el, and these are their names by their courtyards and by their walled camps: twelve chieftains according to their clans.

675.label: Genesis 25:17
675.text: And these are the years of Ishʹma·el’s life, a hundred and thirty-seven years. Then he expired and died and was gathered to his people.

676.label: Genesis 25:18
676.text: And they took up tabernacling from Havʹi·lah near Shur, which is in front of Egypt, as far as As·syrʹi·a. In front of all his brothers he settled down.

677.label: Genesis 25:19
677.text: And this is the history of Isaac the son of Abraham. Abraham became father to Isaac.

678.label: Genesis 25:20
678.text: And Isaac happened to be forty years old at his taking Re·bekʹah the daughter of Be·thuʹel the Syrian of Padʹdan-aʹram, the sister of Laʹban the Syrian, as his wife.

679.label: Genesis 25:21
679.text: And Isaac kept on entreating Jehovah especially for his wife, because she was barren; so Jehovah let himself be entreated for him, and Re·bekʹah his wife became pregnant.

680.label: Genesis 25:22
680.text: And the sons within her began to struggle with each other, so that she said: “If this is the way it is, just why am I alive?” With that she went to inquire of Jehovah.

681.label: Genesis 25:23
681.text: And Jehovah proceeded to say to her: “Two nations are in your belly, and two national groups will be separated from your inward parts; and the one national group will be stronger than the other national group, and the older will serve the younger.”

682.label: Genesis 25:24
682.text: Gradually her days came to the full for giving birth, and, look! twins were in her belly.

683.label: Genesis 25:25
683.text: Then the first came out red all over like an official garment of hair; so they called his name Eʹsau.

684.label: Genesis 25:26
684.text: And after that his brother came out and his hand was holding onto the heel of Eʹsau; so he called his name Jacob. And Isaac was sixty years old at her giving them birth.

685.label: Genesis 25:27
685.text: And the boys got bigger, and Eʹsau became a man knowing how to hunt, a man of the field, but Jacob a blameless man, dwelling in tents.

686.label: Genesis 25:28
686.text: And Isaac had love for Eʹsau, because it meant game in his mouth, whereas Re·bekʹah was a lover of Jacob.

687.label: Genesis 25:29
687.text: Once Jacob was boiling up some stew, when Eʹsau came along from the field and he was tired.

688.label: Genesis 25:30
688.text: So Eʹsau said to Jacob: “Quick, please, give me a swallow of the red—the red there, for I am tired!” That is why his name was called Eʹdom.

689.label: Genesis 25:31
689.text: To this Jacob said: “Sell me, first of all, your right as firstborn!”

690.label: Genesis 25:32
690.text: And Eʹsau continued: “Here I am simply going to die, and of what benefit to me is a birthright?”

691.label: Genesis 25:33
691.text: And Jacob added: “Swear to me first of all!” And he proceeded to swear to him and to sell his right as firstborn to Jacob.

692.label: Genesis 25:34
692.text: And Jacob gave Eʹsau bread and lentil stew, and he went to eating and drinking. Then he got up and went his way. So Eʹsau despised the birthright.

693.label: Genesis 26:1
693.text: Now there arose a famine in the land, besides the first famine that occurred in the days of Abraham, so that Isaac directed himself to A·bimʹe·lech, king of the Phi·lisʹtines, to Geʹrar.

694.label: Genesis 26:2
694.text: Then Jehovah appeared to him and said: “Do not go down to Egypt. Tabernacle in the land that I designate to you.

695.label: Genesis 26:3
695.text: Reside as an alien in this land, and I shall continue with you and bless you, because to you and to your seed I shall give all these lands, and I will carry out the sworn statement that I swore to Abraham your father,

696.label: Genesis 26:4
696.text: ‘And I will multiply your seed like the stars of the heavens and I will give to your seed all these lands; and by means of your seed all nations of the earth will certainly bless themselves,’

697.label: Genesis 26:5
697.text: due to the fact that Abraham listened to my voice and continued to keep his obligations to me, my commands, my statutes, and my laws.”

698.label: Genesis 26:6
698.text: So Isaac went on dwelling at Geʹrar.

699.label: Genesis 26:7
699.text: Well, the men of the place kept asking with respect to his wife, and he would say: “She is my sister.” For he was afraid to say “My wife” for fear that, to quote him, “the men of the place should kill me because of Re·bekʹah,” because she was attractive in appearance.

700.label: Genesis 26:8
700.text: So it came about that as his days there extended themselves A·bimʹe·lech, king of the Phi·lisʹtines, was looking out of the window and taking in the sight, and there was Isaac having a good time with Re·bekʹah his wife.

701.label: Genesis 26:9
701.text: At once A·bimʹe·lech called Isaac and said: “Why, she is no other than your wife! So how is it that you said, ‘She is my sister’?” At this Isaac said to him: “I said it for fear I should die on her account.”

702.label: Genesis 26:10
702.text: But A·bimʹe·lech continued: “What is this you have done to us? A little more and certainly one of the people would have lain down with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us!”

703.label: Genesis 26:11
703.text: Then A·bimʹe·lech commanded all the people, saying: “Anybody touching this man and his wife will surely be put to death!”

704.label: Genesis 26:12
704.text: Afterward Isaac began to sow seed in that land, and in that year he was getting up to a hundred measures to one, as Jehovah was blessing him.

705.label: Genesis 26:13
705.text: Consequently the man became great and went on advancing more and more and growing great until he got very great.

706.label: Genesis 26:14
706.text: And he came to have flocks of sheep and herds of cattle and a large body of servants, so that the Phi·lisʹtines began to envy him.

707.label: Genesis 26:15
707.text: As for all the wells that the servants of his father had dug in the days of Abraham his father, these the Phi·lisʹtines stopped up and they would fill them with dry earth.

708.label: Genesis 26:16
708.text: Finally A·bimʹe·lech said to Isaac: “Move from our neighborhood, because you have grown far stronger than we are.”

709.label: Genesis 26:17
709.text: So Isaac moved from there and encamped in the torrent valley of Geʹrar and took up dwelling there.

710.label: Genesis 26:18
710.text: And Isaac proceeded to dig again the wells of water that they had dug in the days of Abraham his father but which the Phi·lisʹtines went stopping up after Abraham’s death; and he resumed calling their names by the names that his father had called them.

711.label: Genesis 26:19
711.text: And the servants of Isaac went on digging in the torrent valley and so they found there a well of fresh water.

712.label: Genesis 26:20
712.text: And the shepherds of Geʹrar fell to quarreling with the shepherds of Isaac, saying: “The water is ours!” Hence he called the name of the well Eʹsek, because they had contended with him.

713.label: Genesis 26:21
713.text: And they went digging another well, and they fell to quarreling over it also. Hence he called its name Sitʹnah.

714.label: Genesis 26:22
714.text: Later he moved away from there and dug another well, but they did not quarrel over it. Hence he called its name Re·hoʹboth and said: “It is because now Jehovah has given us ample room and has made us fruitful in the earth.”

715.label: Genesis 26:23
715.text: Then he went up from there to Beʹer-sheʹba.

716.label: Genesis 26:24
716.text: And Jehovah proceeded to appear to him during that night and to say: “I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not be afraid, because I am with you, and I will bless you and multiply your seed on account of Abraham my servant.”

717.label: Genesis 26:25
717.text: Accordingly he built an altar there and called on the name of Jehovah and pitched his tent there, and the servants of Isaac went excavating a well there.

718.label: Genesis 26:26
718.text: Later on A·bimʹe·lech came to him from Geʹrar with A·huzʹzath his confidential friend and Phiʹcol the chief of his army.

719.label: Genesis 26:27
719.text: At this Isaac said to them: “Why have YOU come to me, seeing that YOU yourselves hated me and so sent me away from YOUR neighborhood?”

720.label: Genesis 26:28
720.text: To this they said: “We have unmistakably seen that Jehovah has proved to be with you. Hence we said, ‘Let, please, an oath of obligation occur between us, between us and you, and let us conclude a covenant with you,

721.label: Genesis 26:29
721.text: that you will do nothing bad toward us just as we have not touched you and just as we have done only good toward you in that we sent you away in peace. You now are the blessed of Jehovah.’”

722.label: Genesis 26:30
722.text: Then he made a feast for them and they ate and drank.

723.label: Genesis 26:31
723.text: Next morning they were early in rising and they made sworn statements one to the other. After that Isaac sent them away and they went from him in peace.

724.label: Genesis 26:32
724.text: Now on that day it occurred that the servants of Isaac proceeded to come and report to him regarding the well that they had dug, and to say to him: “We have found water!”

725.label: Genesis 26:33
725.text: Hence he called its name Shiʹbah. That is why the name of the city is Beʹer-sheʹba, down to this day.

726.label: Genesis 26:34
726.text: And Eʹsau grew to be forty years old. Then he took as wife Juʹdith the daughter of Be·eʹri the Hitʹtite and also Basʹe·math the daughter of Eʹlon the Hitʹtite.

727.label: Genesis 26:35
727.text: And they were a source of bitterness of spirit to Isaac and Re·bekʹah.

728.label: Genesis 27:1
728.text: Now it came about that when Isaac was old and his eyes were too dim to see he then called Eʹsau his older son and said to him: “My son!” at which he said to him: “Here I am!”

729.label: Genesis 27:2
729.text: And he went on to say: “Here, now, I have become old. I do not know the day of my death.

730.label: Genesis 27:3
730.text: So at this time take, please, your implements, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt some venison for me.

731.label: Genesis 27:4
731.text: Then make me a tasty dish such as I am fond of and bring it to me and, ah, let me eat, in order that my soul may bless you before I die.”

732.label: Genesis 27:5
732.text: However, Re·bekʹah was listening while Isaac spoke to Eʹsau his son. And Eʹsau went on out into the field to hunt game and to bring it in.

733.label: Genesis 27:6
733.text: And Re·bekʹah said to Jacob her son: “Here I just heard your father speaking to Eʹsau your brother, saying,

734.label: Genesis 27:7
734.text: ‘Bring me some game and make me a tasty dish and, ah, let me eat, that I may bless you before Jehovah before my death.’

735.label: Genesis 27:8
735.text: And now, my son, listen to my voice in what I am commanding you.

736.label: Genesis 27:9
736.text: Go, please, to the herd and get me from there two kids of the goats, good ones, that I may make them up into a tasty dish for your father such as he is fond of.

737.label: Genesis 27:10
737.text: Then you must bring it to your father and he must eat it, in order that he may bless you before his death.”

738.label: Genesis 27:11
738.text: And Jacob proceeded to say to Re·bekʹah his mother: “But Eʹsau my brother is a hairy man and I am a smooth man.

739.label: Genesis 27:12
739.text: What if my father feels me? Then I shall certainly become in his eyes like one making a mockery, and I shall certainly bring upon myself a malediction and not a blessing.”

740.label: Genesis 27:13
740.text: At this his mother said to him: “Upon me be the malediction meant for you, my son. Only listen to my voice and go, get them for me.”

741.label: Genesis 27:14
741.text: Accordingly he went and got them and brought them to his mother, and his mother made a tasty dish such as his father was fond of.

742.label: Genesis 27:15
742.text: After that Re·bekʹah took garments of Eʹsau her older son, the most desirable ones which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob her younger son.

743.label: Genesis 27:16
743.text: And the skins of the kids of the goats she put upon his hands and upon the hairless part of his neck.

744.label: Genesis 27:17
744.text: Then she gave the tasty dish and the bread that she had made into the hand of Jacob her son.

745.label: Genesis 27:18
745.text: So he went on in to his father and said: “My father!” to which he said: “Here I am! Who are you, my son?”

746.label: Genesis 27:19
746.text: And Jacob went on to say to his father: “I am Eʹsau your firstborn. I have done just as you have spoken to me. Raise yourself up, please. Sit down and eat some of my game, in order that your soul may bless me.”

747.label: Genesis 27:20
747.text: At that Isaac said to his son: “How is it that you have been so quick in finding it, my son?” In turn he said: “Because Jehovah your God caused it to meet up with me.”

748.label: Genesis 27:21
748.text: Then Isaac said to Jacob: “Come near, please, that I may feel you, my son, to know whether you are really my son Eʹsau or not.”

749.label: Genesis 27:22
749.text: So Jacob came near to Isaac his father, and he went feeling him, after which he said: “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Eʹsau.”

750.label: Genesis 27:23
750.text: And he did not recognize him, because his hands proved to be hairy like the hands of Eʹsau his brother. Hence he blessed him.

751.label: Genesis 27:24
751.text: After that he said: “You are really my son Eʹsau?” to which he said: “I am.”

752.label: Genesis 27:25
752.text: Then he said: “Bring it near to me that I may eat some of the game of my son, to the end that my soul may bless you.” With that he brought it near to him and he began to eat, and he brought him wine and he began to drink.

753.label: Genesis 27:26
753.text: Then Isaac his father said to him: “Come near, please, and kiss me, my son.”

754.label: Genesis 27:27
754.text: So he came near and kissed him, and he could smell the scent of his garments. And he proceeded to bless him and to say: “See, the scent of my son is like the scent of the field which Jehovah has blessed.

755.label: Genesis 27:28
755.text: And may the [true] God give you the dews of the heavens and the fertile soils of the earth and an abundance of grain and new wine.

756.label: Genesis 27:29
756.text: Let peoples serve you and let national groups bow low to you. Become master over your brothers, and let the sons of your mother bow low to you. Cursed be each one of those cursing you, and blessed be each one of those blessing you.”

757.label: Genesis 27:30
757.text: Now it came about as soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, yes, it indeed came about when Jacob had barely come out from before the face of Isaac his father, that Eʹsau his brother came back from his hunting.

758.label: Genesis 27:31
758.text: And he too went about making a tasty dish. Then he brought it to his father and said to his father: “Let my father get up and eat some of his son’s game, in order that your soul may bless me.”

759.label: Genesis 27:32
759.text: At this Isaac his father said to him: “Who are you?” to which he said: “I am your son, your firstborn, Eʹsau.”

760.label: Genesis 27:33
760.text: And Isaac began to shake with a great trembling in extreme measure, and so he said: “Who, then, was it that hunted for game and came bringing it to me, so that I ate of everything before you could come in and I blessed him? Blessed too he will become!”

761.label: Genesis 27:34
761.text: On hearing his father’s words Eʹsau began to cry out in an extremely loud and bitter manner and to say to his father: “Bless me, even me too, my father!”

762.label: Genesis 27:35
762.text: But he went on to say: “Your brother came with deception that he might get the blessing meant for you.”

763.label: Genesis 27:36
763.text: At this he said: “Is that not why his name is called Jacob, in that he should supplant me these two times? My birthright he has already taken, and here at this time he has taken my blessing!” Then he added: “Have you not reserved a blessing for me?”

764.label: Genesis 27:37
764.text: But in answer to Eʹsau Isaac continued: “Here I have appointed him master over you, and all his brothers I have given to him as servants, and grain and new wine I have bestowed for his support, and where is there anything I can do for you, my son?”

765.label: Genesis 27:38
765.text: Then Eʹsau said to his father: “Is there just one blessing that you have, my father? Bless me, even me too, my father!” With that Eʹsau raised his voice and burst into tears.

766.label: Genesis 27:39
766.text: So in answer Isaac his father said to him: “Behold, away from the fertile soils of the earth your dwelling will be found, and away from the dew of the heavens above.

767.label: Genesis 27:40
767.text: And by your sword you will live, and your brother you will serve. But it will certainly occur that, when you grow restless, you will indeed break his yoke off your neck.”

768.label: Genesis 27:41
768.text: However, Eʹsau harbored animosity for Jacob on account of the blessing with which his father had blessed him, and Eʹsau kept saying in his heart: “The days of the period of mourning for my father are getting closer. After that I am going to kill Jacob my brother.”

769.label: Genesis 27:42
769.text: When the words of Eʹsau her older son were told to Re·bekʹah, she at once sent and called Jacob her younger son and said to him: “Look! Eʹsau your brother is comforting himself in regard to you—to kill you.

770.label: Genesis 27:43
770.text: Now, then, my son, listen to my voice and get up, run away to Laʹban my brother at Haʹran.

771.label: Genesis 27:44
771.text: And you must dwell with him for some days until the rage of your brother calms down,

772.label: Genesis 27:45
772.text: until the anger of your brother turns away from you and he has forgotten what you have done to him. And I shall certainly send and get you from there. Why should I be bereaved also of both of YOU in one day?”

773.label: Genesis 27:46
773.text: After that Re·bekʹah kept saying to Isaac: “I have come to abhor this life of mine because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob ever takes a wife from the daughters of Heth like these from the daughters of the land, of what good is life to me?”

774.label: Genesis 28:1
774.text: Consequently Isaac called Jacob and blessed him and commanded him and said to him: “You must not take a wife from the daughters of Caʹnaan.

775.label: Genesis 28:2
775.text: Get up, go to Padʹdan-aʹram to the house of Be·thuʹel the father of your mother and from there take yourself a wife from the daughters of Laʹban the brother of your mother.

776.label: Genesis 28:3
776.text: And God Almighty will bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and you will certainly become a congregation of peoples.

777.label: Genesis 28:4
777.text: And he will give to you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your seed with you, that you may take possession of the land of your alien residences, which God has given to Abraham.”

778.label: Genesis 28:5
778.text: So Isaac sent Jacob away, and he struck out for Padʹdan-aʹram, for Laʹban the son of Be·thuʹel the Syrian, the brother of Re·bekʹah, mother of Jacob and Eʹsau.

779.label: Genesis 28:6
779.text: When Eʹsau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and had sent him away to Padʹdan-aʹram to take from there a wife for himself, and that when he blessed him he laid the command upon him, saying: “Do not take a wife from the daughters of Caʹnaan”;

780.label: Genesis 28:7
780.text: and that Jacob was obeying his father and his mother and was on his way to Padʹdan-aʹram;

781.label: Genesis 28:8
781.text: then Eʹsau saw that the daughters of Caʹnaan were displeasing in the eyes of Isaac his father.

782.label: Genesis 28:9
782.text: Hence Eʹsau went to Ishʹma·el and took as wife Maʹha·lath the daughter of Ishʹma·el the son of Abraham, the sister of Ne·baʹioth, besides his other wives.

783.label: Genesis 28:10
783.text: And Jacob continued on his way out from Beʹer-sheʹba and kept going to Haʹran.

784.label: Genesis 28:11
784.text: In time he came across a place and set about spending the night there because the sun had set. So he took one of the stones of the place and set it as his head supporter and lay down in that place.

785.label: Genesis 28:12
785.text: And he began to dream, and, look! there was a ladder stationed upon the earth and its top reaching up to the heavens; and, look! there were God’s angels ascending and descending on it.

786.label: Genesis 28:13
786.text: And, look! there was Jehovah stationed above it, and he proceeded to say: “I am Jehovah the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land upon which you are lying, to you I am going to give it and to your seed.

787.label: Genesis 28:14
787.text: And your seed will certainly become like the dust particles of the earth, and you will certainly spread abroad to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south, and by means of you and by means of your seed all the families of the ground will certainly bless themselves.

788.label: Genesis 28:15
788.text: And here I am with you and I will keep you in all the way you are going and I will return you to this ground, because I am not going to leave you until I have actually done what I have spoken to you.”

789.label: Genesis 28:16
789.text: Then Jacob awoke from his sleep and said: “Truly Jehovah is in this place and I myself did not know it.”

790.label: Genesis 28:17
790.text: And he grew fearful and added: “How fear-inspiring this place is! This is nothing else but the house of God and this is the gate of the heavens.”

791.label: Genesis 28:18
791.text: So Jacob got up early in the morning and took the stone that was there as his head supporter and he set it up as a pillar and poured oil on the top of it.

792.label: Genesis 28:19
792.text: Further, he called the name of that place Bethʹel; but the fact is, Luz was the city’s name formerly.

793.label: Genesis 28:20
793.text: And Jacob went on to vow a vow, saying: “If God will continue with me and will certainly keep me on this way on which I am going and will certainly give me bread to eat and garments to wear

794.label: Genesis 28:21
794.text: and I shall certainly return in peace to the house of my father, then Jehovah will have proved to be my God.

795.label: Genesis 28:22
795.text: And this stone that I have set up as a pillar will become a house of God, and as for everything that you will give me I shall without fail give the tenth of it to you.”

796.label: Genesis 29:1
796.text: After that Jacob set his feet in motion and traveled on to the land of the Orientals.

797.label: Genesis 29:2
797.text: Now he looked, and here there was a well in the field and here three droves of sheep were lying down there by it, because from that well they were accustomed to water the droves; and there was a great stone over the mouth of the well.

798.label: Genesis 29:3
798.text: When all the droves had been gathered there, they rolled away the stone from off the mouth of the well, and they watered the flocks, after which they returned the stone over the mouth of the well to its place.

799.label: Genesis 29:4
799.text: So Jacob said to them: “My brothers, from what place are YOU?” to which they said: “We are from Haʹran.”

800.label: Genesis 29:5
800.text: Then he said to them: “Do YOU know Laʹban the grandson of Naʹhor?” to which they said: “We know him.”

801.label: Genesis 29:6
801.text: At this he said to them: “Is it all right with him?” In turn they said: “It is all right. And here is Rachel his daughter coming with the sheep!”

802.label: Genesis 29:7
802.text: And he went on to say: “Why, it is yet full day. It is not the time for gathering the herds. WATER the sheep, then go feed them.”

803.label: Genesis 29:8
803.text: To this they said: “We are not allowed to do so until all the droves are gathered and they actually roll away the stone from off the mouth of the well. Then we must water the sheep.”

804.label: Genesis 29:9
804.text: While he was yet speaking with them, Rachel came with the sheep that belonged to her father, for she was a shepherdess.

805.label: Genesis 29:10
805.text: And it came about that when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laʹban his mother’s brother and the sheep of Laʹban his mother’s brother, Jacob immediately approached and rolled away the stone from off the mouth of the well and watered the sheep of Laʹban his mother’s brother.

806.label: Genesis 29:11
806.text: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and raised his voice and burst into tears.

807.label: Genesis 29:12
807.text: And Jacob began to tell Rachel that he was the brother of her father and that he was the son of Re·bekʹah. And she went running and telling her father.

808.label: Genesis 29:13
808.text: Now it came about that as soon as Laʹban heard the report about Jacob the son of his sister, he went running to meet him. Then he embraced him and kissed him and brought him on into his house. And he began to relate to Laʹban all these things.

809.label: Genesis 29:14
809.text: After that Laʹban said to him: “You are indeed my bone and my flesh.” So he dwelt with him a full month.

810.label: Genesis 29:15
810.text: After that Laʹban said to Jacob: “Are you my brother, and must you serve me for nothing? Tell me, What are your wages to be?”

811.label: Genesis 29:16
811.text: As it was, Laʹban had two daughters. The name of the older was Leʹah and the name of the younger Rachel.

812.label: Genesis 29:17
812.text: But the eyes of Leʹah had no luster, whereas Rachel had become beautiful in form and beautiful of countenance.

813.label: Genesis 29:18
813.text: And Jacob was in love with Rachel. So he said: “I am willing to serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.”

814.label: Genesis 29:19
814.text: To this Laʹban said: “It is better for me to give her to you than for me to give her to another man. Keep dwelling with me.”

815.label: Genesis 29:20
815.text: And Jacob proceeded to serve seven years for Rachel, but in his eyes they proved to be like some few days because of his love for her.

816.label: Genesis 29:21
816.text: Then Jacob said to Laʹban: “Give over my wife, because my days are up, and let me have relations with her.”

817.label: Genesis 29:22
817.text: With that Laʹban gathered all the men of the place and made a feast.

818.label: Genesis 29:23
818.text: But it turned out that during the evening he resorted to taking Leʹah his daughter and bringing her to him that he might have relations with her.

819.label: Genesis 29:24
819.text: Moreover, Laʹban gave to her Zilʹpah his maidservant, even to Leʹah his daughter, as a maidservant.

820.label: Genesis 29:25
820.text: So it followed in the morning that here it was Leʹah! Consequently he said to Laʹban: “What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel that I served with you? So why have you tricked me?”

821.label: Genesis 29:26
821.text: To this Laʹban said: “It is not customary to do this way in our place, to give the younger woman before the firstborn.

822.label: Genesis 29:27
822.text: Celebrate to the full the week of this woman. After that there shall be given to you also this other woman for the service that you can serve with me for seven years more.”

823.label: Genesis 29:28
823.text: Accordingly Jacob did so and celebrated fully the week of this woman, after which he gave him Rachel his daughter as his wife.

824.label: Genesis 29:29
824.text: Besides, Laʹban gave Bilʹhah his maidservant to Rachel his daughter as her maidservant.

825.label: Genesis 29:30
825.text: Then he had relations also with Rachel and also expressed more love for Rachel than for Leʹah, and he went serving with him for yet seven years more.

826.label: Genesis 29:31
826.text: When Jehovah came to see that Leʹah was hated, he then opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.

827.label: Genesis 29:32
827.text: And Leʹah became pregnant and brought a son to birth and then called his name Reuʹben, for she said: “It is because Jehovah has looked upon my wretchedness, in that now my husband will begin to love me.”

828.label: Genesis 29:33
828.text: And she became pregnant again and brought a son to birth and then said: “It is because Jehovah has listened, in that I was hated and so he gave me also this one.” Hence she called his name Simʹe·on.

829.label: Genesis 29:34
829.text: And she became pregnant yet again and brought a son to birth and then said: “Now this time my husband will join himself to me, because I have borne him three sons.” His name was therefore called Leʹvi.

830.label: Genesis 29:35
830.text: And she became pregnant once more and brought a son to birth and then said: “This time I shall laud Jehovah.” She therefore called his name Judah. After that she left off giving birth.

831.label: Genesis 30:1
831.text: When Rachel came to see that she had borne nothing to Jacob, Rachel got jealous of her sister and began to say to Jacob: “Give me children or otherwise I shall be a dead woman.”

832.label: Genesis 30:2
832.text: At this Jacob’s anger burned against Rachel and he said: “Am I in the place of God, who has held back the fruit of the belly from you?”

833.label: Genesis 30:3
833.text: So she said: “Here is my slave girl Bilʹhah. Have relations with her, that she may give birth upon my knees and that I, even I, may get children from her.”

834.label: Genesis 30:4
834.text: With that she gave him Bilʹhah her maidservant as wife, and Jacob had relations with her.

835.label: Genesis 30:5
835.text: And Bilʹhah became pregnant and in time bore Jacob a son.

836.label: Genesis 30:6
836.text: Then Rachel said: “God has acted as my judge and has also listened to my voice, so that he gave me a son.” That is why she called his name Dan.

837.label: Genesis 30:7
837.text: And Bilʹhah, Rachel’s maidservant, became pregnant once more and in time bore a second son to Jacob.

838.label: Genesis 30:8
838.text: Then Rachel said: “With strenuous wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister. I have also come off winner!” So she called his name Naphʹta·li.

839.label: Genesis 30:9
839.text: When Leʹah came to see that she had left off giving birth, she proceeded to take Zilʹpah her maidservant and to give her to Jacob as wife.

840.label: Genesis 30:10
840.text: In time Zilʹpah, Leʹah’s maidservant, bore a son to Jacob.

841.label: Genesis 30:11
841.text: Then Leʹah said: “With good fortune!” So she called his name Gad.

842.label: Genesis 30:12
842.text: After that Zilʹpah, Leʹah’s maidservant, bore a second son to Jacob.

843.label: Genesis 30:13
843.text: Then Leʹah said: “With my happiness! For the daughters will certainly pronounce me happy.” So she called his name Ashʹer.

844.label: Genesis 30:14
844.text: Now Reuʹben went walking in the days of the wheat harvest and got to find mandrakes in the field. So he brought them to Leʹah his mother. Then Rachel said to Leʹah: “Give me, please, some of your son’s mandrakes.”

845.label: Genesis 30:15
845.text: At this she said to her: “Is this a little thing, your having taken my husband, with your now taking also my son’s mandrakes?” So Rachel said: “For that reason he is going to lie down with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”

846.label: Genesis 30:16
846.text: When Jacob was coming from the field in the evening, Leʹah went on out to meet him and then said: “It is with me you are going to have relations, because I have hired you outright with my son’s mandrakes.” Accordingly he lay down with her that night.

847.label: Genesis 30:17
847.text: And God heard and answered Leʹah and she became pregnant and in time bore to Jacob a fifth son.

848.label: Genesis 30:18
848.text: Then Leʹah said: “God has given me a hireling’s wages, because I have given my maidservant to my husband.” So she called his name Isʹsa·char.

849.label: Genesis 30:19
849.text: And Leʹah became pregnant once more and in time bore a sixth son to Jacob.

850.label: Genesis 30:20
850.text: Then Leʹah said: “God has endowed me, yes, me, with a good endowment. At last my husband will tolerate me, because I have borne him six sons.” So she called his name Zebʹu·lun.

851.label: Genesis 30:21
851.text: And afterward she bore a daughter and then called her name Diʹnah.

852.label: Genesis 30:22
852.text: Finally God remembered Rachel, and God heard and answered her in that he opened her womb.

853.label: Genesis 30:23
853.text: And she became pregnant and brought a son to birth. Then she said: “God has taken away my reproach!”

854.label: Genesis 30:24
854.text: So she called his name Joseph, saying: “Jehovah is adding another son to me.”

855.label: Genesis 30:25
855.text: And it followed that when Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob immediately said to Laʹban: “Send me away that I may go to my place and to my country.

856.label: Genesis 30:26
856.text: Give over my wives and my children, for whom I have served with you, that I may go; for you yourself must know my service which I have rendered you.”

857.label: Genesis 30:27
857.text: Then Laʹban said to him: “If, now, I have found favor in your eyes,—I have taken the omens to the effect that Jehovah is blessing me due to you.”

858.label: Genesis 30:28
858.text: And he added: “Stipulate your wages to me and I shall give them.”

859.label: Genesis 30:29
859.text: So he said to him: “You yourself must know how I have served you and how your herd has fared with me;

860.label: Genesis 30:30
860.text: that it was little that you actually had before my coming, and it went expanding to a multitude, in that Jehovah blessed you since I stepped in. So now when am I to do something also for my own house?”

861.label: Genesis 30:31
861.text: Then he said: “What shall I give you?” And Jacob went on to say: “You will give me nothing whatsoever! If you will do this thing for me, I shall resume shepherding your flock. I shall continue guarding it.

862.label: Genesis 30:32
862.text: I will pass among your whole flock today. You set aside from there every sheep speckled and with color patches, and every dark-brown sheep among the young rams and any color-patched and speckled one among the she-goats. Hereafter such must be my wages.

863.label: Genesis 30:33
863.text: And my right-doing must answer for me on whatever future day you may come to look over my wages; every one that is not speckled and color-patched among the she-goats and dark brown among the young rams is something stolen if it is with me.”

864.label: Genesis 30:34
864.text: To this Laʹban said: “Why, that is fine! Let it be according to your word.”

865.label: Genesis 30:35
865.text: Then he set aside on that day the he-goats striped and color-patched and all the she-goats speckled and color-patched, every one in which there was any white and every one dark brown among the young rams, but he gave them over into the hands of his sons.

866.label: Genesis 30:36
866.text: After that he set a distance of three days’ journey between himself and Jacob, and Jacob was shepherding the flocks of Laʹban that remained over.

867.label: Genesis 30:37
867.text: Then Jacob took for his use staffs still moist of the storax tree and of the almond tree and of the plane tree and peeled in them white peeled spots by laying bare white places which were upon the staffs.

868.label: Genesis 30:38
868.text: Finally the staffs that he had peeled he placed in front of the flock, in the gutters, in the water drinking troughs, where the flocks would come to drink, that they might get into a heat before them when they came to drink.

869.label: Genesis 30:39
869.text: Consequently the flocks would get in heat before the staffs, and the flocks would produce striped, speckled and color-patched ones.

870.label: Genesis 30:40
870.text: And Jacob separated the young rams and then turned the faces of the flocks to the striped ones and all the dark-brown ones among the flocks of Laʹban. Then he set his own droves by themselves and did not set them by the flocks of Laʹban.

871.label: Genesis 30:41
871.text: And it always occurred that whenever the robust flocks would get in heat, Jacob would locate the staffs in the gutters before the eyes of the flocks, that they might get in heat by the staffs.

872.label: Genesis 30:42
872.text: But when the flocks showed feebleness he would not locate them there. So the feeble ones always came to be Laʹban’s, but the robust ones Jacob’s.

873.label: Genesis 30:43
873.text: And the man went on increasing more and more, and great flocks and maidservants and menservants and camels and asses came to be his.

874.label: Genesis 31:1
874.text: In time he got to hear the words of the sons of Laʹban, saying: “Jacob has taken everything that belonged to our father; and from what belonged to our father he has amassed all this wealth.”

875.label: Genesis 31:2
875.text: When Jacob would look at the face of Laʹban, here it was not with him as formerly.

876.label: Genesis 31:3
876.text: Finally Jehovah said to Jacob: “Return to the land of your fathers and to your relatives, and I shall continue with you.”

877.label: Genesis 31:4
877.text: Then Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leʹah out to the field to his flock,

878.label: Genesis 31:5
878.text: and he said to them: “I am seeing the face of YOUR father, that he is not the same toward me as formerly; but the God of my father has proved to be with me.

879.label: Genesis 31:6
879.text: And YOU yourselves certainly know that with all my power I have served YOUR father.

880.label: Genesis 31:7
880.text: And YOUR father has trifled with me and he has changed my wages ten times, but God has not allowed him to do me harm.

881.label: Genesis 31:8
881.text: If on the one hand he would say, ‘The speckled ones will become your wages,’ then the whole flock produced speckled ones; but if on the other hand he would say, ‘The striped ones will become your wages,’ then the whole flock produced striped ones.

882.label: Genesis 31:9
882.text: So God kept taking the herd of YOUR father away and giving it to me.

883.label: Genesis 31:10
883.text: At last it came about at the time when the flock got in heat that I raised my eyes and saw a sight in a dream and here the he-goats springing upon the flock were striped, speckled and spotty.

884.label: Genesis 31:11
884.text: Then the angel of the [true] God said to me in the dream, ‘Jacob!’ to which I said, ‘Here I am.’

885.label: Genesis 31:12
885.text: And he continued, ‘Raise your eyes, please, and see all the he-goats springing upon the flock are striped, speckled and spotty, for I have seen all that Laʹban is doing to you.

886.label: Genesis 31:13
886.text: I am the [true] God of Bethʹel, where you anointed a pillar and where you vowed a vow to me. Now get up, go out of this land and return to the land of your birth.’”

887.label: Genesis 31:14
887.text: At this Rachel and Leʹah answered and said to him: “Is there a share of inheritance for us anymore in the house of our father?

888.label: Genesis 31:15
888.text: Are we not really considered as foreigners to him since he has sold us, so that he keeps eating continually even from the money given for us?

889.label: Genesis 31:16
889.text: For all the riches that God has taken away from our father are ours and our children’s. So now everything God has said to you do.”

890.label: Genesis 31:17
890.text: Then Jacob got up and lifted his children and his wives onto the camels;

891.label: Genesis 31:18
891.text: and he began driving all his herd and all the goods that he had accumulated, the herd of his acquisition that he had accumulated in Padʹdan-aʹram, in order to go to Isaac his father to the land of Caʹnaan.

892.label: Genesis 31:19
892.text: Now Laʹban had gone to shear his sheep. Meantime Rachel stole the teraphim that belonged to her father.

893.label: Genesis 31:20
893.text: So Jacob outwitted Laʹban the Syrian, because he had not told him that he was running away.

894.label: Genesis 31:21
894.text: And he proceeded to run away and to get up and cross the River, he and all he had. After that he directed his face to the mountainous region of Gilʹe·ad.

895.label: Genesis 31:22
895.text: Later, on the third day, it was told to Laʹban that Jacob had run away.

896.label: Genesis 31:23
896.text: With that he took his brothers with him and went chasing after him for a distance of seven days’ journey and caught up with him in the mountainous region of Gilʹe·ad.

897.label: Genesis 31:24
897.text: Then God came to Laʹban the Syrian in a dream by night and said to him: “Watch yourself that you do not go speaking either good or bad with Jacob.”

898.label: Genesis 31:25
898.text: So Laʹban approached Jacob, as Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain and Laʹban had encamped his brothers in the mountainous region of Gilʹe·ad.

899.label: Genesis 31:26
