899.text: Then Laʹban said to Jacob: “What have you done, in that you resorted to outwitting me and driving my daughters off like captives taken by the sword?

900.label: Genesis 31:27
900.text: Why did you have to run away secretly and outwit me and not tell me, that I might send you away with rejoicing and with songs, with tambourine and with harp?

901.label: Genesis 31:28
901.text: And you did not give me a chance to kiss my children and my daughters. Now you have acted foolishly.

902.label: Genesis 31:29
902.text: It is in the power of my hand to do harm to YOU people, but the God of YOUR father talked to me last night, saying, ‘Watch yourself against speaking either good or bad with Jacob.’

903.label: Genesis 31:30
903.text: While you have actually gone now because you have been yearning intensely for the house of your father, why, though, have you stolen my gods?”

904.label: Genesis 31:31
904.text: In answer Jacob proceeded to say to Laʹban: “It was because I was afraid. For I said to myself, ‘You might tear your daughters away from me.’

905.label: Genesis 31:32
905.text: Whoever it is with whom you may find your gods, let him not live. Before our brothers, examine for yourself what is with me and take them for yourself.” But Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.

906.label: Genesis 31:33
906.text: So Laʹban went on into the tent of Jacob and into the tent of Leʹah and into the tent of the two slave girls, but did not find them. Finally he went out of Leʹah’s tent and went on into Rachel’s tent.

907.label: Genesis 31:34
907.text: Now Rachel had taken the teraphim, and she resorted to putting them in the woman’s saddle basket of the camel, and she kept sitting upon them. So Laʹban went feeling through the whole tent, but did not find them.

908.label: Genesis 31:35
908.text: Then she said to her father: “Do not let anger gleam in the eyes of my lord, because I am not able to get up before you, for the customary thing with women is upon me.” So he searched on carefully, but did not find the teraphim.

909.label: Genesis 31:36
909.text: And Jacob became angry and began to quarrel with Laʹban, and in answer Jacob went on to say to Laʹban: “What is the revolt on my part, what the sin of mine, as a reason why you have hotly pursued after me?

910.label: Genesis 31:37
910.text: Now that you have felt through all my goods, what of all the goods of your house have you found? Put it here in front of my brothers and your brothers, and let them decide between us two.

911.label: Genesis 31:38
911.text: These twenty years I have been with you. Your female sheep and your she-goats did not suffer abortions, and the rams of your flock I never ate.

912.label: Genesis 31:39
912.text: Any animal torn to pieces I did not bring to you. I myself would stand the loss of it. Whether one was stolen by day or was stolen by night, you would put in a claim for it from my hand.

913.label: Genesis 31:40
913.text: It has been my experience that by day the heat consumed me and the cold by night, and my sleep would flee from my eyes.

914.label: Genesis 31:41
914.text: This makes twenty years for me in your house. I have served you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flock, and you kept changing my wages ten times.

915.label: Genesis 31:42
915.text: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Dread of Isaac, had not proved on my side, you would now have sent me away empty-handed. My wretchedness and the toil of my hands God has seen, and so he reproved you last night.”

916.label: Genesis 31:43
916.text: Then Laʹban in answer said to Jacob: “The daughters are my daughters and the children my children and the flock my flock, and everything you are looking at is mine and my daughters’. What can I do against these today or against their children whom they have borne?

917.label: Genesis 31:44
917.text: And now, come, let us conclude a covenant, I and you, and it must serve as a witness between me and you.”

918.label: Genesis 31:45
918.text: Accordingly Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.

919.label: Genesis 31:46
919.text: Then Jacob said to his brothers: “Pick up stones!” And they went taking stones and making a heap. After that they ate there on the heap.

920.label: Genesis 31:47
920.text: And Laʹban began calling it Jeʹgar-sa·ha·duʹtha, but Jacob called it Galʹe·ed.

921.label: Genesis 31:48
921.text: And Laʹban proceeded to say: “This heap is a witness between me and you today.” That is why he called its name Galʹe·ed,

922.label: Genesis 31:49
922.text: and The Watchtower, because he said: “Let Jehovah keep watch between me and you when we are situated unseen the one from the other.

923.label: Genesis 31:50
923.text: If you go to afflicting my daughters and if you go to taking wives in addition to my daughters, there is no man with us. See! God is a witness between me and you.”

924.label: Genesis 31:51
924.text: And Laʹban went on to say to Jacob: “Here is this heap and here is the pillar that I have erected between me and you.

925.label: Genesis 31:52
925.text: This heap is a witness, and the pillar is something that bears witness, that I will not pass this heap against you and that you will not pass this heap and this pillar against me for harm.

926.label: Genesis 31:53
926.text: Let the god of Abraham and the god of Naʹhor judge between us, the god of their father.” But Jacob swore by the Dread of his father Isaac.

927.label: Genesis 31:54
927.text: After that Jacob sacrificed a sacrifice in the mountain and invited his brothers to eat bread. Accordingly they ate bread and passed the night in the mountain.

928.label: Genesis 31:55
928.text: However, Laʹban got up early in the morning and kissed his children and his daughters and blessed them. Then Laʹban got on his way that he might return to his own place.

929.label: Genesis 32:1
929.text: And as for Jacob, he got on his way, and the angels of God now met up with him.

930.label: Genesis 32:2
930.text: Immediately Jacob said, when he saw them: “The camp of God this is!” Hence he called the name of that place Ma·ha·naʹim.

931.label: Genesis 32:3
931.text: Then Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to Eʹsau his brother to the land of Seʹir, the field of Eʹdom,

932.label: Genesis 32:4
932.text: and he commanded them, saying: “This is what YOU will say to my lord, to Eʹsau, ‘This is what your servant Jacob has said: “With Laʹban I have resided as an alien and I have stayed for a long time till now.

933.label: Genesis 32:5
933.text: And I have come to have bulls and asses, sheep, and menservants and maidservants, and I would like to send to notify my lord, that I may find favor in your eyes.”’”

934.label: Genesis 32:6
934.text: In time the messengers returned to Jacob, saying: “We got to your brother Eʹsau, and he is also on his way to meet you, and four hundred men with him.”

935.label: Genesis 32:7
935.text: And Jacob became very much afraid and grew anxious. So he divided the people who were with him, and the flocks and the cattle and the camels into two camps,

936.label: Genesis 32:8
936.text: and he said: “If Eʹsau should come to the one camp and assault it, then there is certain to be a camp remaining to make an escape.”

937.label: Genesis 32:9
937.text: After that Jacob said: “O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O Jehovah, you who are saying to me, ‘Return to your land and to your relatives and I will deal well with you,’

938.label: Genesis 32:10
938.text: I am unworthy of all the loving-kindnesses and of all the faithfulness that you have exercised toward your servant, for with but my staff I crossed this Jordan and now I have become two camps.

939.label: Genesis 32:11
939.text: Deliver me, I pray you, from my brother’s hand, from Eʹsau’s hand, because I am afraid of him that he may come and certainly assault me, mother together with children.

940.label: Genesis 32:12
940.text: And you, you have said, ‘Unquestionably I shall deal well with you and I will constitute your seed like the grains of sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.’”

941.label: Genesis 32:13
941.text: And he kept lodging there on that night. And from what came to his hand he proceeded to take a gift for Eʹsau his brother:

942.label: Genesis 32:14
942.text: two hundred she-goats and twenty he-goats, two hundred female sheep and twenty rams,

943.label: Genesis 32:15
943.text: thirty camels giving suck and their young ones, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty she-asses and ten full-grown asses.

944.label: Genesis 32:16
944.text: Then he handed over to his servants one drove after another by itself and repeatedly said to his servants: “Cross over ahead of me, and YOU are to set an interval between drove and drove.”

945.label: Genesis 32:17
945.text: Further he commanded the first one, saying: “In case that Eʹsau my brother should meet you and ask you, saying, ‘To whom do you belong, and where are you going and to whom do these ahead of you belong?’

946.label: Genesis 32:18
946.text: then you must say, ‘To your servant, to Jacob. A gift it is, sent to my lord, to Eʹsau, and look! he himself is also behind us.’”

947.label: Genesis 32:19
947.text: And he went on to command also the second, also the third, also all those following the droves, saying: “According to this word YOU are to speak to Eʹsau on YOUR encountering him.

948.label: Genesis 32:20
948.text: And YOU must say also, ‘Here is your servant Jacob behind us.’” For he said to himself: “I may appease him by the gift going ahead of me, and afterward I shall see his face. Perhaps he will give a kindly reception.”

949.label: Genesis 32:21
949.text: So the gift went crossing over ahead of him, but he himself lodged that night in the camp.

950.label: Genesis 32:22
950.text: Later during that night he rose and took his two wives and his two maidservants and his eleven young sons and crossed over the ford of Jabʹbok.

951.label: Genesis 32:23
951.text: So he took them and brought them over the torrent valley, and he brought over what he had.

952.label: Genesis 32:24
952.text: Finally Jacob was left by himself. Then a man began to grapple with him until the dawn ascended.

953.label: Genesis 32:25
953.text: When he got to see that he had not prevailed over him, then he touched the socket of his thigh joint; and the socket of Jacob’s thigh joint got out of place during his grappling with him.

954.label: Genesis 32:26
954.text: After that he said: “Let me go, for the dawn has ascended.” To this he said: “I am not going to let you go until you first bless me.”

955.label: Genesis 32:27
955.text: So he said to him: “What is your name?” to which he said: “Jacob.”

956.label: Genesis 32:28
956.text: Then he said: “Your name will no longer be called Jacob but Israel, for you have contended with God and with men so that you at last prevailed.”

957.label: Genesis 32:29
957.text: In turn Jacob inquired and said: “Tell me, please, your name.” However, he said: “Why is it that you inquire for my name?” With that he blessed him there.

958.label: Genesis 32:30
958.text: Hence Jacob called the name of the place Pe·niʹel, because, to quote him, “I have seen God face to face and yet my soul was delivered.”

959.label: Genesis 32:31
959.text: And the sun began to flash upon him as soon as he passed by Pe·nuʹel, but he was limping upon his thigh.

960.label: Genesis 32:32
960.text: That is why the sons of Israel are not accustomed to eat the sinew of the thigh nerve, which is on the socket of the thigh joint, down to this day, because he touched the socket of Jacob’s thigh joint by the sinew of the thigh nerve.

961.label: Genesis 33:1
961.text: In time Jacob raised his eyes and looked, and here Eʹsau was coming and with him four hundred men. Consequently he divided off the children to Leʹah and to Rachel and to the two maidservants,

962.label: Genesis 33:2
962.text: and he put the maidservants and their children foremost and Leʹah and her children after them and Rachel and Joseph to the rear of them.

963.label: Genesis 33:3
963.text: And he himself passed on ahead of them and proceeded to bow down to the earth seven times until he got near to his brother.

964.label: Genesis 33:4
964.text: And Eʹsau went running to meet him, and he began to embrace him and fall upon his neck and kiss him, and they burst into tears.

965.label: Genesis 33:5
965.text: Then he raised his eyes and saw the women and the children and said: “Who are these with you?” to which he said: “The children with whom God has favored your servant.”

966.label: Genesis 33:6
966.text: At that the maidservants came forward, they and their children, and bowed down;

967.label: Genesis 33:7
967.text: and Leʹah too came forward, and her children, and they bowed down, and afterward Joseph came forward, and Rachel, and they bowed down.

968.label: Genesis 33:8
968.text: He now said: “What do you mean by all this camp of travelers that I have met?” To this he said: “In order to find favor in the eyes of my lord.”

969.label: Genesis 33:9
969.text: Then Eʹsau said: “I have a great many, my brother. Let continue yours what is yours.”

970.label: Genesis 33:10
970.text: However, Jacob said: “No, please. If, now, I have found favor in your eyes, then you must take my gift at my hand, because in harmony with its purpose I have seen your face as though seeing God’s face in that you received me with pleasure.

971.label: Genesis 33:11
971.text: Take, please, the gift conveying my blessing which was brought to you, because God has favored me and because I have everything.” And he continued to urge him, so that he took it.

972.label: Genesis 33:12
972.text: Later on he said: “Let us pull out and go, and let me go in advance of you.”

973.label: Genesis 33:13
973.text: But he said to him: “My lord is aware that the children are delicate and sheep and cattle that are giving suck are in my charge, and should they drive them too quickly for one day, then the whole flock will certainly die.

974.label: Genesis 33:14
974.text: Let my lord, please, pass on ahead of his servant, but may I myself continue the journey at my leisure according to the pace of the livestock that is before me and according to the pace of the children until I shall come to my lord at Seʹir.”

975.label: Genesis 33:15
975.text: Then Eʹsau said: “Let me, please, put at your disposal some of the people who are with me.” To this he said: “Why this? Let me find favor in the eyes of my lord.”

976.label: Genesis 33:16
976.text: So on that day Eʹsau turned back on his way to Seʹir.

977.label: Genesis 33:17
977.text: And Jacob pulled out for Sucʹcoth, and he proceeded to build himself a house and for his herd he made booths. That was why he called the name of the place Sucʹcoth.

978.label: Genesis 33:18
978.text: In time Jacob came safe and sound to the city of Sheʹchem, which is in the land of Caʹnaan, while he was coming from Padʹdan-aʹram; and he pitched camp in front of the city.

979.label: Genesis 33:19
979.text: Then he acquired a tract of the field where he pitched his tent at the hand of the sons of Haʹmor the father of Sheʹchem, for a hundred pieces of money.

980.label: Genesis 33:20
980.text: After that he set up there an altar and called it God the God of Israel.

981.label: Genesis 34:1
981.text: Now Diʹnah the daughter of Leʹah, whom she had borne to Jacob, used to go out to see the daughters of the land.

982.label: Genesis 34:2
982.text: And Sheʹchem the son of Haʹmor the Hiʹvite, a chieftain of the land, got to see her and then took her and lay down with her and violated her.

983.label: Genesis 34:3
983.text: And his soul began clinging to Diʹnah the daughter of Jacob, and he fell in love with the young woman and kept speaking persuasively to the young woman.

984.label: Genesis 34:4
984.text: Finally Sheʹchem said to Haʹmor his father: “Get me this young lady as a wife.”

985.label: Genesis 34:5
985.text: And Jacob heard that he had defiled Diʹnah his daughter. And his sons happened to be with his herd in the field; and Jacob kept silent until they should come in.

986.label: Genesis 34:6
986.text: Later Haʹmor, Sheʹchem’s father, went out to Jacob to speak with him.

987.label: Genesis 34:7
987.text: And the sons of Jacob came in from the field as soon as they heard of it; and the men became hurt in their feelings and they grew very angry, because he had committed a disgraceful folly against Israel in lying down with Jacob’s daughter, whereas nothing like that ought to be done.

988.label: Genesis 34:8
988.text: And Haʹmor proceeded to speak with them, saying: “As for Sheʹchem my son, his soul is attached to YOUR daughter. Give her, please, to him as a wife,

989.label: Genesis 34:9
989.text: and form marriage alliances with us. YOUR daughters YOU are to give to us, and our daughters YOU are to take for yourselves.

990.label: Genesis 34:10
990.text: And with us YOU may dwell, and the land will become available for YOU. Dwell and carry on business in it and get settled in it.”

991.label: Genesis 34:11
991.text: Then Sheʹchem said to her father and to her brothers: “Let me find favor in YOUR eyes, and whatever YOU will say to me I shall give it.

992.label: Genesis 34:12
992.text: Raise very high the marriage money and gift imposed upon me, and I stand willing to give according to what YOU may say to me; only give me the young woman as a wife.”

993.label: Genesis 34:13
993.text: And Jacob’s sons began to answer Sheʹchem and Haʹmor his father with deceit and to speak so because he had defiled Diʹnah their sister.

994.label: Genesis 34:14
994.text: And they went on to say to them: “We cannot possibly do such a thing, to give our sister to a man who has a foreskin, because that is a reproach to us.

995.label: Genesis 34:15
995.text: Only on this condition can we give consent to YOU, that YOU become like us, by every male of YOURS getting circumcised.

996.label: Genesis 34:16
996.text: Then we shall certainly give our daughters to YOU, and YOUR daughters we shall take for ourselves, and we shall certainly dwell with YOU and become one people.

997.label: Genesis 34:17
997.text: But if YOU do not listen to us to get circumcised, then we will take our daughter and go.”

998.label: Genesis 34:18
998.text: And their words seemed good in the eyes of Haʹmor and in the eyes of Sheʹchem, Haʹmor’s son,

999.label: Genesis 34:19
999.text: and the young man did not delay to perform the condition, because he did find delight in Jacob’s daughter and he was the most honorable of the whole house of his father.

1000.label: Genesis 34:20
1000.text: So Haʹmor and Sheʹchem his son went to the gate of their city and began to speak to the men of their city, saying:

1001.label: Genesis 34:21
1001.text: “These men are peace-loving toward us. Hence let them dwell in the land and carry on business in it, as the land is quite wide before them. Their daughters we can take as wives for ourselves and our own daughters we can give to them.

1002.label: Genesis 34:22
1002.text: Only on this condition will the men give us their consent to dwell with us so as to become one people, that every male of ours gets circumcised just the way they are circumcised.

1003.label: Genesis 34:23
1003.text: Then their possessions and their wealth and all their livestock, will they not be ours? Only let us give them our consent that they may dwell with us.”

1004.label: Genesis 34:24
1004.text: Then all those going out by the gate of his city listened to Haʹmor and to Sheʹchem his son, and all the males got circumcised, all those going out by the gate of his city.

1005.label: Genesis 34:25
1005.text: However, it came about that on the third day, when they got to be aching, the two sons of Jacob, Simʹe·on and Leʹvi, brothers of Diʹnah, proceeded to take each one his sword and to go unsuspectedly to the city and to kill every male.

1006.label: Genesis 34:26
1006.text: And Haʹmor and Sheʹchem his son they killed with the edge of the sword. Then they took Diʹnah from Sheʹchem’s house and went on out.

1007.label: Genesis 34:27
1007.text: The other sons of Jacob attacked the fatally wounded men and went plundering the city, because they had defiled their sister.

1008.label: Genesis 34:28
1008.text: Their flocks and their herds and their asses and what was in the city and what was in the field they took.

1009.label: Genesis 34:29
1009.text: And all their means of maintenance and all their little children and their wives they carried off captive, so that they plundered all that was in the houses.

1010.label: Genesis 34:30
1010.text: At this Jacob said to Simʹe·on and to Leʹvi: “YOU have brought ostracism upon me in making me a stench to the inhabitants of the land, with the Caʹnaan·ites and the Perʹiz·zites; whereas I am few in number, and they will certainly gather together against me and assault me and I must be annihilated, I and my house.”

1011.label: Genesis 34:31
1011.text: In turn they said: “Ought anyone to treat our sister like a prostitute?”

1012.label: Genesis 35:1
1012.text: After that God said to Jacob: “Rise, go up to Bethʹel and dwell there, and make an altar there to the [true] God who appeared to you when you were running away from Eʹsau your brother.”

1013.label: Genesis 35:2
1013.text: Then Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him: “Put away the foreign gods that are in the midst of YOU and cleanse yourselves and change YOUR mantles,

1014.label: Genesis 35:3
1014.text: and let us rise and go up to Bethʹel. And there I shall make an altar to the [true] God who answered me in the day of my distress in that he proved to be with me in the way that I have gone.”

1015.label: Genesis 35:4
1015.text: So they gave Jacob all the foreign gods that were in their hands and the earrings that were in their ears, and Jacob hid them under the big tree that was close by Sheʹchem.

1016.label: Genesis 35:5
1016.text: After that they pulled away, and the terror of God came to be upon the cities that were round about them, so that they did not chase after the sons of Jacob.

1017.label: Genesis 35:6
1017.text: Eventually Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Caʹnaan, that is to say, Bethʹel, he and all the people who were with him.

1018.label: Genesis 35:7
1018.text: Then he built an altar there and began to call the place El-bethʹel, because there the [true] God had revealed himself to him at the time of his running away from his brother.

1019.label: Genesis 35:8
1019.text: Later Debʹo·rah the nursing woman of Re·bekʹah died and was buried at the foot of Bethʹel under a massive tree. Hence he called its name Alʹlon-bacʹuth.

1020.label: Genesis 35:9
1020.text: God now appeared to Jacob once again during his coming from Padʹdan-aʹram and blessed him.

1021.label: Genesis 35:10
1021.text: And God went on to say to him: “Your name is Jacob. No longer is your name to be called Jacob, but Israel will your name become.” And he began to call his name Israel.

1022.label: Genesis 35:11
1022.text: And God said further to him: “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and become many. Nations and a congregation of nations will proceed out of you, and kings will come out of your loins.

1023.label: Genesis 35:12
1023.text: As for the land that I have given to Abraham and to Isaac, to you I shall give it, and to your seed after you I shall give the land.”

1024.label: Genesis 35:13
1024.text: After that God went up from above him at the place where he had spoken with him.

1025.label: Genesis 35:14
1025.text: Consequently Jacob stationed a pillar in the place where he had spoken with him, a pillar of stone, and he poured a drink offering upon it and poured oil upon it.

1026.label: Genesis 35:15
1026.text: And Jacob continued to call the name of the place where God had spoken with him Bethʹel.

1027.label: Genesis 35:16
1027.text: Then they pulled away from Bethʹel. And while there was yet a good stretch of land before coming to Ephʹrath, Rachel proceeded to give birth, and it was going hard with her in making the delivery.

1028.label: Genesis 35:17
1028.text: But so it was that while she had difficulty in making the delivery the midwife said to her: “Do not be afraid, for you will have this son also.”

1029.label: Genesis 35:18
1029.text: And the result was that as her soul was going out (because she died) she called his name Ben-oʹni; but his father called him Benjamin.

1030.label: Genesis 35:19
1030.text: Thus Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephʹrath, that is to say, Bethʹle·hem.

1031.label: Genesis 35:20
1031.text: Hence Jacob stationed a pillar over her grave. This is the pillar of Rachel’s grave down to this day.

1032.label: Genesis 35:21
1032.text: After that Israel pulled away and pitched his tent a distance beyond the tower of Eʹder.

1033.label: Genesis 35:22
1033.text: And it came about while Israel was tabernacling in that land that once Reuʹben went and lay down with Bilʹhah his father’s concubine, and Israel got to hear of it. So there came to be twelve sons of Jacob.

1034.label: Genesis 35:23
1034.text: The sons by Leʹah were Jacob’s firstborn Reuʹben and Simʹe·on and Leʹvi and Judah and Isʹsa·char and Zebʹu·lun.

1035.label: Genesis 35:24
1035.text: The sons by Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.

1036.label: Genesis 35:25
1036.text: And the sons by Bilʹhah, Rachel’s maidservant, were Dan and Naphʹta·li.

1037.label: Genesis 35:26
1037.text: And the sons by Zilʹpah, Leʹah’s maidservant, were Gad and Ashʹer. These are Jacob’s sons who were born to him in Padʹdan-aʹram.

1038.label: Genesis 35:27
1038.text: At length Jacob came to Isaac his father to Mamʹre, to Kirʹi·ath-arʹba, that is to say, Heʹbron, where Abraham and also Isaac had resided as aliens.

1039.label: Genesis 35:28
1039.text: And the days of Isaac came to be a hundred and eighty years.

1040.label: Genesis 35:29
1040.text: After that Isaac expired and died and was gathered to his people, old and satisfied with days, and Eʹsau and Jacob his sons buried him.

1041.label: Genesis 36:1
1041.text: And this is the history of Eʹsau, that is to say, Eʹdom.

1042.label: Genesis 36:2
1042.text: Eʹsau took his wives from the daughters of Caʹnaan: Aʹdah the daughter of Eʹlon the Hitʹtite and O·hol·i·baʹmah the daughter of Aʹnah, the granddaughter of Zibʹe·on the Hiʹvite,

1043.label: Genesis 36:3
1043.text: and Basʹe·math, Ishʹma·el’s daughter, the sister of Ne·baʹioth.

1044.label: Genesis 36:4
1044.text: And Aʹdah proceeded to bear Elʹi·phaz to Eʹsau, and Basʹe·math bore Reuʹel,

1045.label: Genesis 36:5
1045.text: and O·hol·i·baʹmah bore Jeʹush and Jaʹlam and Koʹrah. These are the sons of Eʹsau who were born to him in the land of Caʹnaan.

1046.label: Genesis 36:6
1046.text: After that Eʹsau took his wives and his sons and his daughters and all the souls of his house and his herd and all his other beasts and all his wealth, which he had accumulated in the land of Caʹnaan, and went to a land away from Jacob his brother,

1047.label: Genesis 36:7
1047.text: because their goods had become too great for them to dwell together and the land of their alien residences was not able to sustain them as a result of their herds.

1048.label: Genesis 36:8
1048.text: So Eʹsau took up dwelling in the mountainous region of Seʹir. Eʹsau is Eʹdom.

1049.label: Genesis 36:9
1049.text: And this is the history of Eʹsau the father of Eʹdom in the mountainous region of Seʹir.

1050.label: Genesis 36:10
1050.text: These are the names of the sons of Eʹsau: Elʹi·phaz the son of Aʹdah, Eʹsau’s wife; Reuʹel the son of Basʹe·math, Eʹsau’s wife.

1051.label: Genesis 36:11
1051.text: And the sons of Elʹi·phaz came to be Teʹman, Oʹmar, Zeʹpho and Gaʹtam and Keʹnaz.

1052.label: Genesis 36:12
1052.text: And Timʹna became the concubine of Elʹi·phaz, Eʹsau’s son. In time she bore to Elʹi·phaz Amʹa·lek. These are the sons of Aʹdah, Eʹsau’s wife.

1053.label: Genesis 36:13
1053.text: These are the sons of Reuʹel: Naʹhath and Zeʹrah, Shamʹmah and Mizʹzah. These came to be the sons of Basʹe·math, Eʹsau’s wife.

1054.label: Genesis 36:14
1054.text: And these came to be the sons of O·hol·i·baʹmah the daughter of Aʹnah, the granddaughter of Zibʹe·on, Eʹsau’s wife, in that she bore to Eʹsau Jeʹush and Jaʹlam and Koʹrah.

1055.label: Genesis 36:15
1055.text: These are the sheiks of the sons of Eʹsau: The sons of Elʹi·phaz, Eʹsau’s firstborn: Sheik Teʹman, sheik Oʹmar, sheik Zeʹpho, sheik Keʹnaz,

1056.label: Genesis 36:16
1056.text: sheik Koʹrah, sheik Gaʹtam, sheik Amʹa·lek. These are the sheiks of Elʹi·phaz in the land of Eʹdom. These are the sons by Aʹdah.

1057.label: Genesis 36:17
1057.text: These are the sons of Reuʹel, Eʹsau’s son: Sheik Naʹhath, sheik Zeʹrah, sheik Shamʹmah, sheik Mizʹzah. These are the sheiks of Reuʹel in the land of Eʹdom. These are the sons by Basʹe·math, Eʹsau’s wife.

1058.label: Genesis 36:18
1058.text: Finally these are the sons of O·hol·i·baʹmah, Eʹsau’s wife: Sheik Jeʹush, sheik Jaʹlam, sheik Koʹrah. These are the sheiks of O·hol·i·baʹmah the daughter of Aʹnah, Eʹsau’s wife.

1059.label: Genesis 36:19
1059.text: These are the sons of Eʹsau, and these are their sheiks. He is Eʹdom.

1060.label: Genesis 36:20
1060.text: These are the sons of Seʹir the Horʹite, the inhabitants of the land: Loʹtan and Shoʹbal and Zibʹe·on and Aʹnah

1061.label: Genesis 36:21
1061.text: and Diʹshon and Eʹzer and Diʹshan. These are the sheiks of the Horʹite, the sons of Seʹir, in the land of Eʹdom.

1062.label: Genesis 36:22
1062.text: And the sons of Loʹtan came to be Hoʹri and Heʹmam; and Loʹtan’s sister was Timʹna.

1063.label: Genesis 36:23
1063.text: And these are the sons of Shoʹbal: Alʹvan and Manʹa·hath and Eʹbal, Sheʹpho and Oʹnam.

1064.label: Genesis 36:24
1064.text: And these are the sons of Zibʹe·on: Aʹiah and Aʹnah. This is the Aʹnah who found the hot springs in the wilderness while he was tending the asses for Zibʹe·on his father.

1065.label: Genesis 36:25
1065.text: And these are the children of Aʹnah: Diʹshon and O·hol·i·baʹmah the daughter of Aʹnah.

1066.label: Genesis 36:26
1066.text: And these are the sons of Diʹshon: Hemʹdan and Eshʹban and Ithʹran and Cheʹran.

1067.label: Genesis 36:27
1067.text: These are the sons of Eʹzer: Bilʹhan and Zaʹa·van and Aʹkan.

1068.label: Genesis 36:28
1068.text: These are the sons of Diʹshan: Uz and Aʹran.

1069.label: Genesis 36:29
1069.text: These are the sheiks of the Horʹite: Sheik Loʹtan, sheik Shoʹbal, sheik Zibʹe·on, sheik Aʹnah,

1070.label: Genesis 36:30
1070.text: sheik Diʹshon, sheik Eʹzer, sheik Diʹshan. These are the sheiks of the Horʹite according to their sheiks in the land of Seʹir.

1071.label: Genesis 36:31
1071.text: Now these are the kings who reigned in the land of Eʹdom before any king reigned over the sons of Israel.

1072.label: Genesis 36:32
1072.text: And Beʹla son of Beʹor proceeded to reign in Eʹdom, and the name of his city was Dinʹha·bah.

1073.label: Genesis 36:33
1073.text: When Beʹla died, Joʹbab son of Zeʹrah from Bozʹrah began to reign instead of him.

1074.label: Genesis 36:34
1074.text: When Joʹbab died, Huʹsham from the land of the Teʹman·ites began to reign instead of him.

1075.label: Genesis 36:35
1075.text: When Huʹsham died, Haʹdad son of Beʹdad, who defeated the Midʹi·an·ites in the field of Moʹab, began to reign instead of him, and the name of his city was Aʹvith.

1076.label: Genesis 36:36
1076.text: When Haʹdad died, Samʹlah from Mas·reʹkah began to reign instead of him.

1077.label: Genesis 36:37
1077.text: When Samʹlah died, Shaʹul from Re·hoʹboth by the River began to reign instead of him.

1078.label: Genesis 36:38
1078.text: When Shaʹul died, Baʹal-haʹnan son of Achʹbor began to reign instead of him.

1079.label: Genesis 36:39
1079.text: When Baʹal-haʹnan son of Achʹbor died, Haʹdar began to reign instead of him; and the name of his city was Paʹu, and the name of his wife was Me·hetʹa·bel the daughter of Maʹtred the daughter of Meʹza·hab.

1080.label: Genesis 36:40
1080.text: So these are the names of the sheiks of Eʹsau according to their families, according to their places, by their names: Sheik Timʹna, sheik Alʹvah, sheik Jeʹtheth,

1081.label: Genesis 36:41
1081.text: sheik O·hol·i·baʹmah, sheik Eʹlah, sheik Piʹnon,

1082.label: Genesis 36:42
1082.text: sheik Keʹnaz, sheik Teʹman, sheik Mibʹzar,

1083.label: Genesis 36:43
1083.text: sheik Magʹdi·el, sheik Iʹram. These are the sheiks of Eʹdom according to their dwellings in the land of their possession. This is Eʹsau the father of Eʹdom.

1084.label: Genesis 37:1
1084.text: And Jacob continued to dwell in the land of the alien residences of his father, in the land of Caʹnaan.

1085.label: Genesis 37:2
1085.text: This is the history of Jacob. Joseph, when seventeen years old, happened to be tending sheep with his brothers among the flock, and, being but a boy, he was with the sons of Bilʹhah and the sons of Zilʹpah, the wives of his father. So Joseph brought a bad report about them to their father.

1086.label: Genesis 37:3
1086.text: And Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons, because he was the son of his old age; and he had a long, striped shirtlike garment made for him.

1087.label: Genesis 37:4
1087.text: When his brothers came to see that their father loved him more than all his brothers, they began to hate him, and they were not able to speak peacefully to him.

1088.label: Genesis 37:5
1088.text: Later on Joseph had a dream and told it to his brothers, and they found further reason to hate him.

1089.label: Genesis 37:6
1089.text: And he went on to say to them: “Listen, please, to this dream that I have dreamed.

1090.label: Genesis 37:7
1090.text: Well, here we were binding sheaves in the middle of the field when here my sheaf got up and also stood erect and here YOUR sheaves proceeded to encircle and bow down to my sheaf.”

1091.label: Genesis 37:8
1091.text: And his brothers began to say to him: “Are you going to be king over us for certain? or, Are you going to dominate over us for certain?” So they found fresh reason to hate him over his dreams and over his words.

1092.label: Genesis 37:9
1092.text: After that he had still another dream, and he related it to his brothers and said: “Here I have had a dream once more, and here the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”

1093.label: Genesis 37:10
1093.text: Then he related it to his father as well as his brothers, and his father began to rebuke him and say to him: “What does this dream that you have dreamed mean? Am I and also your mother and your brothers for certain going to come and bow down to the earth to you?”

1094.label: Genesis 37:11
1094.text: And his brothers grew jealous of him, but his father observed the saying.

1095.label: Genesis 37:12
1095.text: His brothers now went to feed the flock of their father close by Sheʹchem.

1096.label: Genesis 37:13
1096.text: After a while Israel said to Joseph: “Your brothers are tending [flocks] close by Sheʹchem, are they not? Come, and let me send you to them.” At this he said to him: “Here I am!”

1097.label: Genesis 37:14
1097.text: So he said to him: “Go, please. See whether your brothers are safe and sound and whether the flock is safe and sound, and bring me back word.” With that he sent him away from the low plain of Heʹbron, and he went on toward Sheʹchem.

1098.label: Genesis 37:15
1098.text: Later a man found him and here he was wandering in a field. Then the man inquired of him, saying: “What are you looking for?”

1099.label: Genesis 37:16
1099.text: To this he said: “It is my brothers I am looking for. Tell me, please, Where are they tending flocks?”

1100.label: Genesis 37:17
1100.text: And the man continued: “They have pulled away from here, because I heard them saying, ‘Let us go to Doʹthan.’” So Joseph kept on after his brothers and found them at Doʹthan.

1101.label: Genesis 37:18
1101.text: Well, they caught sight of him from a distance, and before he could get close by them they began plotting cunningly against him to put him to death.

1102.label: Genesis 37:19
1102.text: So they said to one another: “Look! Here comes that dreamer.

1103.label: Genesis 37:20
1103.text: And now come and let us kill him and pitch him into one of the waterpits; and we must say a vicious wild beast devoured him. Then let us see what will become of his dreams.”

1104.label: Genesis 37:21
1104.text: When Reuʹben heard this he tried to deliver him out of their hand. So he said: “Let us not strike his soul fatally.”

1105.label: Genesis 37:22
1105.text: And Reuʹben went on to say to them: “Do not spill blood. Pitch him into this waterpit which is in the wilderness and do not lay a violent hand upon him.” His purpose was to deliver him out of their hand in order to return him to his father.

1106.label: Genesis 37:23
1106.text: So it came about that as soon as Joseph came to his brothers, they went stripping Joseph of his long garment, even the long striped garment that was upon him;

1107.label: Genesis 37:24
1107.text: after which they took him and pitched him into the waterpit. At the time the pit was empty; there was no water in it.

1108.label: Genesis 37:25
1108.text: Then they sat down to eat bread. When they raised their eyes and took a look, why, here was a caravan of Ishʹma·el·ites that was coming from Gilʹe·ad, and their camels were carrying labdanum and balsam and resinous bark, on their way to take it down to Egypt.

1109.label: Genesis 37:26
1109.text: At this Judah said to his brothers: “What profit would there be in case we killed our brother and did cover over his blood?

1110.label: Genesis 37:27
1110.text: Come and let us sell him to the Ishʹma·el·ites, and do not let our hand be upon him. After all, he is our brother, our flesh.” So they listened to their brother.

1111.label: Genesis 37:28
1111.text: Now men, Midʹi·an·ite merchants, went passing by. Hence they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the waterpit and then sold Joseph to the Ishʹma·el·ites for twenty silver pieces. Eventually these brought Joseph into Egypt.

1112.label: Genesis 37:29
1112.text: Later Reuʹben returned to the waterpit and here Joseph was not in the waterpit. Consequently he ripped his garments apart.

1113.label: Genesis 37:30
1113.text: When he returned to his other brothers he exclaimed: “The child is gone! And I—where am I really to go?”

1114.label: Genesis 37:31
1114.text: However, they took Joseph’s long garment and slaughtered a male goat and repeatedly dipped the long garment in the blood.

1115.label: Genesis 37:32
1115.text: After that they sent the long striped garment and had it brought to their father and said: “This is what we found. Examine, please, whether it is your son’s long garment or not.”

1116.label: Genesis 37:33
1116.text: And he went examining it and exclaimed: “It is my son’s long garment! A vicious wild beast must have devoured him! Joseph is surely torn to pieces!”

1117.label: Genesis 37:34
1117.text: With that Jacob ripped his mantles apart and put sackcloth upon his hips and carried on mourning over his son for many days.

1118.label: Genesis 37:35
1118.text: And all his sons and all his daughters kept rising up to comfort him, but he kept refusing to take comfort and saying: “For I shall go down mourning to my son into Sheʹol!” And his father continued weeping for him.

1119.label: Genesis 37:36
1119.text: However, the Midʹi·an·ites sold him into Egypt to Potʹi·phar a court official of Pharʹaoh, the chief of the bodyguard.

1120.label: Genesis 38:1
1120.text: Now in the meantime it came about that when Judah went down from his brothers he pitched [his tent] near a man, an A·dulʹlam·ite, and his name was Hiʹrah.

1121.label: Genesis 38:2
1121.text: And there Judah got to see a daughter of a certain Caʹnaan·ite, and his name was Shuʹa. So he took her and had relations with her.

1122.label: Genesis 38:3
1122.text: And she became pregnant. Later she bore a son and he called his name Er.

1123.label: Genesis 38:4
1123.text: Again she became pregnant. In time she bore a son and called his name Oʹnan.

1124.label: Genesis 38:5
1124.text: Yet another time she went on to bear a son and then called his name Sheʹlah. Now he happened to be in Achʹzib at the time she bore him.

1125.label: Genesis 38:6
1125.text: In time Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Taʹmar.

1126.label: Genesis 38:7
1126.text: But Er, Judah’s firstborn, proved to be bad in the eyes of Jehovah; hence Jehovah put him to death.

1127.label: Genesis 38:8
1127.text: In view of that Judah said to Oʹnan: “Have relations with your brother’s wife and perform brother-in-law marriage with her and raise up offspring for your brother.”

1128.label: Genesis 38:9
1128.text: But Oʹnan knew that the offspring would not become his; and it occurred that when he did have relations with his brother’s wife he wasted his semen on the earth so as not to give offspring to his brother.

1129.label: Genesis 38:10
1129.text: Now what he did was bad in the eyes of Jehovah; hence he put him also to death.

1130.label: Genesis 38:11
1130.text: So Judah said to Taʹmar his daughter-in-law: “Dwell as a widow in the house of your father until Sheʹlah my son grows up.” For he said to himself: “He too may die like his brothers.” Accordingly Taʹmar went and continued to dwell at her own father’s house.

1131.label: Genesis 38:12
1131.text: Thus the days became many and the daughter of Shuʹa, Judah’s wife, died; and Judah kept the period of mourning. After that he went up to the shearers of his sheep, he and Hiʹrah his companion the A·dulʹlam·ite, to Timʹnah.

1132.label: Genesis 38:13
1132.text: Then it was told to Taʹmar: “Here your father-in-law is going up to Timʹnah to shear his sheep.”

1133.label: Genesis 38:14
1133.text: With that she removed the garments of her widowhood from her and covered herself with a shawl and veiled herself and sat down at the entrance of E·naʹim, which is along the road to Timʹnah. For she saw that Sheʹlah had grown up and yet she had not been given as a wife to him.

1134.label: Genesis 38:15
1134.text: When Judah caught sight of her, he at once took her for a harlot, because she had covered her face.

1135.label: Genesis 38:16
1135.text: So he turned aside to her by the road and said: “Allow me, please, to have relations with you.” For he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. However, she said: “What will you give me that you may have relations with me?”

1136.label: Genesis 38:17
1136.text: To this he said: “I myself shall send a kid of the goats from the herd.” But she said: “Will you give a security until you send it?”

1137.label: Genesis 38:18
1137.text: And he continued: “What is the security that I shall give you?” to which she said: “Your seal ring and your cord and your rod that is in your hand.” Then he gave them to her and had relations with her, so that she became pregnant by him.

1138.label: Genesis 38:19
1138.text: After that she got up and went and removed her shawl off her and clothed herself with the garments of her widowhood.

1139.label: Genesis 38:20
1139.text: And Judah proceeded to send the kid of the goats by the hand of his companion the A·dulʹlam·ite in order to get back the security from the hand of the woman, but he never found her.

1140.label: Genesis 38:21
1140.text: And he went inquiring of the men of her place, saying: “Where is that temple prostitute in E·naʹim along the road?” But they kept saying: “No temple prostitute has ever been in this place.”

1141.label: Genesis 38:22
1141.text: Finally he returned to Judah and said: “I never found her and, besides, the men of the place said, ‘No temple prostitute has ever been in this place.’”

1142.label: Genesis 38:23
1142.text: So Judah said: “Let her take them for herself, in order that we may not fall into contempt. At any rate, I have sent this kid, but you—you never found her.”

1143.label: Genesis 38:24
1143.text: However, about three months later it happened that it was told to Judah: “Taʹmar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot, and here she is also pregnant by her harlotry.” At that Judah said: “BRING her out and let her be burned.”

1144.label: Genesis 38:25
1144.text: As she was being brought out she herself sent to her father-in-law, saying: “By the man to whom these belong I am pregnant.” And she added: “Examine, please, to whom these belong, the seal ring and the cord and the rod.”

1145.label: Genesis 38:26
1145.text: Then Judah examined them and said: “She is more righteous than I am, for the reason that I did not give her to Sheʹlah my son.” And he had no further intercourse with her after that.

1146.label: Genesis 38:27
1146.text: Now it developed that in the time of her giving birth, why, here there were twins in her belly.

1147.label: Genesis 38:28
1147.text: Further, it turned out that when she was giving birth one extended his hand, and the midwife at once took and tied a scarlet piece about his hand, saying: “This one came out first.”

1148.label: Genesis 38:29
1148.text: Finally it developed that as soon as he drew back his hand, why, here his brother came out, so that she exclaimed: “What do you mean by this, that you have produced a perineal rupture for yourself?” Hence his name was called Peʹrez.

1149.label: Genesis 38:30
1149.text: And afterward his brother upon whose hand the scarlet piece was came out and his name came to be called Zeʹrah.

1150.label: Genesis 39:1
1150.text: As for Joseph, he was brought down to Egypt, and Potʹi·phar, a court official of Pharʹaoh, the chief of the bodyguard, an Egyptian, got to buy him from the hand of the Ishʹma·el·ites who had brought him down there.

1151.label: Genesis 39:2
1151.text: But Jehovah proved to be with Joseph, so that he turned out a successful man and came to be over the house of his master, the Egyptian.

1152.label: Genesis 39:3
1152.text: And his master got to see that Jehovah was with him and that everything he was doing Jehovah was making turn out successful in his hand.

1153.label: Genesis 39:4
1153.text: And Joseph kept finding favor in his eyes and waited upon him continually, so that he appointed him over his house, and all that was his he gave into his hand.

1154.label: Genesis 39:5
1154.text: And it followed that from the time he appointed him over his house and in charge of all that was his Jehovah kept blessing the house of the Egyptian due to Joseph, and Jehovah’s blessing came to be upon all that he had in the house and in the field.

1155.label: Genesis 39:6
1155.text: Finally he left everything that was his in Joseph’s hand; and he did not know what was with him at all except the bread he was eating. Moreover, Joseph grew to be beautiful in form and beautiful in appearance.

1156.label: Genesis 39:7
1156.text: Now after these things it came about that the wife of his master began to raise her eyes toward Joseph and say: “Lie down with me.”

1157.label: Genesis 39:8
1157.text: But he would refuse and would say to his master’s wife: “Here my master does not know what is with me in the house, and everything he has he has given into my hand.

1158.label: Genesis 39:9
1158.text: There is no one greater in this house than I am, and he has not withheld from me anything at all except you, because you are his wife. So how could I commit this great badness and actually sin against God?”

1159.label: Genesis 39:10
1159.text: So it turned out that as she spoke to Joseph day after day he never listened to her to lie alongside her, to continue with her.

1160.label: Genesis 39:11
1160.text: But it happened that on this day as other days he went into the house to do his business, and there was none of the men of the house there in the house.

1161.label: Genesis 39:12
1161.text: Then she grabbed hold of him by his garment, saying: “Lie down with me!” But he left his garment in her hand and took to flight and went on outside.

1162.label: Genesis 39:13
1162.text: So it occurred that as soon as she saw that he had left his garment in her hand that he might flee outside,

1163.label: Genesis 39:14
1163.text: she began to cry out to the men of her house and to say to them: “Look! He brought to us a man, a Hebrew, to make us a laughingstock. He came to me to lie down with me, but I began to cry out at the top of my voice.

1164.label: Genesis 39:15
1164.text: And it followed that as soon as he heard that I raised my voice and began crying out, he then left his garment beside me and took to flight and went on outside.”

1165.label: Genesis 39:16
1165.text: After that she kept his garment laid up beside her until his master came to his house.

1166.label: Genesis 39:17
1166.text: Then she spoke to him according to these words, saying: “The Hebrew servant whom you brought to us came to me to make me a laughingstock.

1167.label: Genesis 39:18
1167.text: But it followed that as soon as I raised my voice and began to cry out, he then left his garment beside me and went fleeing outside.”

1168.label: Genesis 39:19
1168.text: The result was that as soon as his master heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying: “Like this and this your servant did to me,” his anger blazed.

1169.label: Genesis 39:20
1169.text: So Joseph’s master took him and gave him over to the prison house, the place where the prisoners of the king were kept under arrest, and he continued there in the prison house.

1170.label: Genesis 39:21
1170.text: However, Jehovah continued with Joseph and kept extending loving-kindness to him and granting him to find favor in the eyes of the chief officer of the prison house.

1171.label: Genesis 39:22
1171.text: So the chief officer of the prison house gave over into Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison house; and everything that they were doing there he proved to be the one having it done.

1172.label: Genesis 39:23
1172.text: The chief officer of the prison house was looking after absolutely nothing that was in his hand, because Jehovah was with [Joseph] and what he was doing Jehovah was making it turn out successful.

1173.label: Genesis 40:1
1173.text: Now after these things it came about that the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker sinned against their lord the king of Egypt.

1174.label: Genesis 40:2
1174.text: And Pharʹaoh grew indignant at his two officers, at the chief of the cupbearers and at the chief of the bakers.

1175.label: Genesis 40:3
1175.text: So he committed them to the jail of the house of the chief of the bodyguard, to the prison house, the place where Joseph was a prisoner.

1176.label: Genesis 40:4
1176.text: Then the chief of the bodyguard assigned Joseph to be with them that he might wait upon them; and they continued in jail for some days.

1177.label: Genesis 40:5
1177.text: And both of them proceeded to dream a dream, each one his own dream in the one night, each one his dream with its own interpretation, the cupbearer and the baker who belonged to the king of Egypt who were prisoners in the prison house.

1178.label: Genesis 40:6
1178.text: When Joseph came in to them in the morning and saw them, why, here they were looking dejected.

1179.label: Genesis 40:7
1179.text: And he began to inquire of the officers of Pharʹaoh who were with him in the jail of his master’s house, saying: “For what reason are YOUR faces gloomy today?”

1180.label: Genesis 40:8
1180.text: At this they said to him: “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter with us.” So Joseph said to them: “Do not interpretations belong to God? Relate it to me, please.”

1181.label: Genesis 40:9
1181.text: And the chief of the cupbearers went on to relate his dream to Joseph and to say to him: “In my dream, why, here there was a vine before me.

1182.label: Genesis 40:10
1182.text: And on the vine there were three twigs, and it was apparently sprouting shoots. Its blossoms pushed forth. Its clusters ripened their grapes.

1183.label: Genesis 40:11
1183.text: And Pharʹaoh’s cup was in my hand, and I proceeded to take the grapes and squeeze them out into Pharʹaoh’s cup. After that I gave the cup into Pharʹaoh’s hand.”

1184.label: Genesis 40:12
1184.text: Then Joseph said to him: “This is its interpretation: The three twigs are three days.

1185.label: Genesis 40:13
1185.text: In three days from now Pharʹaoh will lift up your head and he will certainly return you to your office; and you will certainly give Pharʹaoh’s cup into his hand, according to the former custom when you acted as his cupbearer.

1186.label: Genesis 40:14
1186.text: Nevertheless, you must keep me in your remembrance as soon as it goes well with you, and you must, please, perform loving-kindness with me and mention me to Pharʹaoh, and you must get me out of this house.

1187.label: Genesis 40:15
1187.text: For I was in fact kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews; and here also I have done nothing at all for which they should put me in the prison hole.”

1188.label: Genesis 40:16
1188.text: When the chief of the bakers saw that he had interpreted something good, he, in turn, said to Joseph: “I too was in my dream, and here there were three baskets of white bread upon my head,

1189.label: Genesis 40:17
1189.text: and in the topmost basket there were all sorts of eatables for Pharʹaoh, the product of a baker, and there were fowls eating them out of the basket on top of my head.”

1190.label: Genesis 40:18
1190.text: Then Joseph answered and said: “This is its interpretation: The three baskets are three days.

1191.label: Genesis 40:19
1191.text: In three days from now Pharʹaoh will lift up your head from off you and will certainly hang you upon a stake; and the fowls will certainly eat your flesh from off you.”

1192.label: Genesis 40:20
1192.text: Now on the third day it turned out to be Pharʹaoh’s birthday, and he proceeded to make a feast for all his servants and to lift up the head of the chief of the cupbearers and the head of the chief of the bakers in the midst of his servants.

1193.label: Genesis 40:21
1193.text: Accordingly he returned the chief of the cupbearers to his post of cupbearer, and he continued to give the cup into Pharʹaoh’s hand.

1194.label: Genesis 40:22
1194.text: But the chief of the bakers he hung up, just as Joseph had given them the interpretation.

1195.label: Genesis 40:23
1195.text: However, the chief of the cupbearers did not remember Joseph and went on forgetting him.

1196.label: Genesis 41:1
1196.text: And it came about at the end of two full years that Pharʹaoh was dreaming and here he was standing by the river Nile.

1197.label: Genesis 41:2
1197.text: And here ascending out of the river Nile were seven cows beautiful in appearance and fat-fleshed, and they went feeding among the Nile grass.

1198.label: Genesis 41:3
1198.text: And here there were seven other cows ascending after them out of the river Nile, ugly in appearance and thin-fleshed, and they took their stand alongside the cows by the bank of the river Nile.

1199.label: Genesis 41:4
1199.text: Then the cows that were ugly in appearance and thin-fleshed began to eat up the seven cows that were beautiful in appearance and fat. At this Pharʹaoh woke up.

1200.label: Genesis 41:5
1200.text: However, he went back to sleep and dreamed a second time. And here there were seven ears of grain coming up on one stalk, fat and good.

1201.label: Genesis 41:6
1201.text: And here there were seven ears of grain, thin and scorched by the east wind, growing up after them.

1202.label: Genesis 41:7
1202.text: And the thin ears of grain began to swallow up the seven fat and full ears of grain. At this Pharʹaoh woke up and here it was a dream.

1203.label: Genesis 41:8
1203.text: And it developed in the morning that his spirit became agitated. So he sent and called all the magic-practicing priests of Egypt and all her wise men, and Pharʹaoh went on to relate his dreams to them. But there was no interpreter of them for Pharʹaoh.

1204.label: Genesis 41:9
1204.text: Then the chief of the cupbearers spoke with Pharʹaoh, saying: “My sins I am mentioning today.

1205.label: Genesis 41:10
1205.text: Pharʹaoh was indignant at his servants. So he committed me to the jail of the house of the chief of the bodyguard, both me and the chief of the bakers.

1206.label: Genesis 41:11
1206.text: After that we both dreamed a dream in the one night, both I and he. We dreamed each one his dream with its own interpretation.

1207.label: Genesis 41:12
1207.text: And there was with us there a young man, a Hebrew, a servant of the chief of the bodyguard. When we related them to him, he proceeded to interpret our dreams to us. He interpreted to each according to his dream.

1208.label: Genesis 41:13
1208.text: And it turned out that just as he had interpreted to us so it happened. Me he returned to my office, but him he hanged.”

1209.label: Genesis 41:14
1209.text: And Pharʹaoh proceeded to send and to call Joseph, that they might bring him quickly from the prison hole. Hence he shaved and changed his mantles and went in to Pharʹaoh.

1210.label: Genesis 41:15
1210.text: Then Pharʹaoh said to Joseph: “I have dreamed a dream, but there is no interpreter of it. Now I myself have heard it said about you that you can hear a dream and interpret it.”

1211.label: Genesis 41:16
1211.text: At this Joseph answered Pharʹaoh, saying: “I need not be considered! God will announce welfare to Pharʹaoh.”

1212.label: Genesis 41:17
1212.text: And Pharʹaoh went on to speak to Joseph: “In my dream here I was standing on the bank of the river Nile.

1213.label: Genesis 41:18
1213.text: And here ascending out of the river Nile were seven cows fat-fleshed and beautiful in form, and they began to feed among the Nile grass.

1214.label: Genesis 41:19
1214.text: And here there were seven other cows ascending after them, poor and very bad in form and thin-fleshed. For badness I have not seen the like of them in all the land of Egypt.

1215.label: Genesis 41:20
1215.text: And the skinny and bad cows began to eat up the first seven fat cows.

1216.label: Genesis 41:21
1216.text: So these came into their bellies, and yet it could not be known that they had come into their bellies, as their appearance was bad just as at the start. At that I woke up.

1217.label: Genesis 41:22
1217.text: “After that I saw in my dream and here there were seven ears of grain coming up on one stalk, full and good.

1218.label: Genesis 41:23
1218.text: And here there were seven ears of grain shriveled, thin, scorched by the east wind, growing up after them.

1219.label: Genesis 41:24
1219.text: And the thin ears of grain began to swallow up the seven good ears of grain. So I stated it to the magic-practicing priests, but there was none telling me.”

1220.label: Genesis 41:25
1220.text: Then Joseph said to Pharʹaoh: “The dream of Pharʹaoh is but one. What the [true] God is doing he has told to Pharʹaoh.

1221.label: Genesis 41:26
1221.text: The seven good cows are seven years. Likewise the seven good ears of grain are seven years. The dream is but one.

1222.label: Genesis 41:27
1222.text: And the seven skinny and bad cows that came up after them are seven years; and the seven empty ears of grain, scorched by the east wind, will prove to be seven years of famine.

1223.label: Genesis 41:28
1223.text: This is the thing that I have spoken to Pharʹaoh: What the [true] God is doing he has caused Pharʹaoh to see.

1224.label: Genesis 41:29
1224.text: “Here there are seven years coming with great plenty in all the land of Egypt.

1225.label: Genesis 41:30
1225.text: But seven years of famine will certainly arise after them, and all the plenty in the land of Egypt will certainly be forgotten and the famine will simply consume the land.

1226.label: Genesis 41:31
1226.text: And the plenty once in the land will not be known as a result of that famine afterward, because it will certainly be very severe.

1227.label: Genesis 41:32
1227.text: And the fact that the dream was repeated to Pharʹaoh twice means that the thing is firmly established on the part of the [true] God, and the [true] God is speeding to do it.

1228.label: Genesis 41:33
1228.text: “So now let Pharʹaoh look for a man discreet and wise and set him over the land of Egypt.

1229.label: Genesis 41:34
1229.text: Let Pharʹaoh act and appoint overseers over the land, and he must take up one fifth of the land of Egypt during the seven years of plenty.

1230.label: Genesis 41:35
1230.text: And let them collect all the foodstuffs of these coming good years, and let them pile up grain under Pharʹaoh’s hand as foodstuffs in the cities, and they must safeguard it.

1231.label: Genesis 41:36
1231.text: And the foodstuffs must serve as a supply for the land for the seven famine years, which will develop in the land of Egypt, in order that the land may not be cut off by the famine.”

1232.label: Genesis 41:37
1232.text: Well, the thing proved to be good in the eyes of Pharʹaoh and of all his servants.

1233.label: Genesis 41:38
1233.text: So Pharʹaoh said to his servants: “Can another man be found like this one in whom the spirit of God is?”

1234.label: Genesis 41:39
1234.text: After that Pharʹaoh said to Joseph: “Since God has caused you to know all this, there is no one as discreet and wise as you are.

1235.label: Genesis 41:40
1235.text: You will personally be over my house, and all my people will obey you implicitly. Only as to the throne shall I be greater than you.”

1236.label: Genesis 41:41
1236.text: And Pharʹaoh added to Joseph: “See, I do place you over all the land of Egypt.”

1237.label: Genesis 41:42
1237.text: With that Pharʹaoh removed his signet ring from his own hand and put it upon Joseph’s hand and clothed him with garments of fine linen and placed a necklace of gold about his neck.

1238.label: Genesis 41:43
1238.text: Moreover, he had him ride in the second chariot of honor that he had, so that they should call out ahead of him, “A·vrékh!” thus putting him over all the land of Egypt.

1239.label: Genesis 41:44
1239.text: And Pharʹaoh further said to Joseph: “I am Pharʹaoh, but without your authorization no man may lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”

1240.label: Genesis 41:45
1240.text: After that Pharʹaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphʹe·nath-pa·neʹah and gave him Asʹe·nath the daughter of Pot·iʹphe·ra the priest of On as a wife. And Joseph began to go out over the land of Egypt.

1241.label: Genesis 41:46
1241.text: And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharʹaoh the king of Egypt. Then Joseph went out from before Pharʹaoh and toured about in all the land of Egypt.

1242.label: Genesis 41:47
1242.text: And during the seven years of plenty the land went on producing by the handfuls.

1243.label: Genesis 41:48
1243.text: And he kept collecting all the foodstuffs of the seven years that came upon the land of Egypt and he would put the foodstuffs in the cities. The foodstuffs of the field that was round about a city he put in the midst of it.

1244.label: Genesis 41:49
1244.text: And Joseph continued piling up grain in very great quantity, like the sand of the sea, until finally they gave up counting it, because it was without number.

1245.label: Genesis 41:50
1245.text: And before the year of the famine arrived there were born to Joseph two sons, whom Asʹe·nath the daughter of Pot·iʹphe·ra the priest of On bore to him.

1246.label: Genesis 41:51
1246.text: So Joseph called the name of the firstborn Ma·nasʹseh, because, to quote him, “God has made me forget all my trouble and all the house of my father.”

1247.label: Genesis 41:52
1247.text: And the name of the second he called Eʹphra·im, because, to quote him, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my wretchedness.”

1248.label: Genesis 41:53
1248.text: And the seven years of the plenty that had obtained in the land of Egypt gradually ended,

1249.label: Genesis 41:54
1249.text: and, in turn, the seven years of the famine started to come, just as Joseph had said. And the famine developed in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was found bread.

1250.label: Genesis 41:55
1250.text: Finally all the land of Egypt became famished and the people began to cry to Pharʹaoh for bread. Then Pharʹaoh said to all the Egyptians: “Go to Joseph. Whatever he says to YOU, YOU are to do.”

1251.label: Genesis 41:56
1251.text: And the famine obtained over all the surface of the earth. Then Joseph began to open up all the grain depositories that were among them and to sell to the Egyptians, as the famine got a strong grip on the land of Egypt.

1252.label: Genesis 41:57
1252.text: Moreover, people of all the earth came to Egypt to buy from Joseph, because the famine had a strong grip on all the earth.

1253.label: Genesis 42:1
1253.text: Eventually Jacob got to see that there were cereals in Egypt. Then Jacob said to his sons: “Why do YOU keep looking at one another?”

1254.label: Genesis 42:2
1254.text: And he added: “Here I have heard that there are cereals in Egypt. Go down there and buy for us from there, that we may keep alive and not die off.”

1255.label: Genesis 42:3
1255.text: Accordingly ten brothers of Joseph went down to buy grain from Egypt.

1256.label: Genesis 42:4
1256.text: But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his other brothers, because he said: “Otherwise a fatal accident may befall him.”

1257.label: Genesis 42:5
1257.text: So Israel’s sons came along with the others who were coming to buy, because the famine existed in the land of Caʹnaan.

1258.label: Genesis 42:6
1258.text: And Joseph was the man in power over the land. He was the one that did the selling to all people of the earth. Consequently Joseph’s brothers came and bowed low to him with their faces to the earth.

1259.label: Genesis 42:7
1259.text: When Joseph got to see his brothers, he at once recognized them, but he made himself unrecognizable to them. So he spoke harshly with them and said to them: “Where have YOU come from?” to which they said: “From the land of Caʹnaan to buy foodstuffs.”

1260.label: Genesis 42:8
1260.text: Thus Joseph recognized his brothers, but they themselves did not recognize him.

1261.label: Genesis 42:9
1261.text: Immediately Joseph remembered the dreams that he had dreamed respecting them, and he went on to say to them: “YOU are spies! YOU have come to see the exposed condition of the land!”

1262.label: Genesis 42:10
1262.text: Then they said to him: “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy foodstuffs.

1263.label: Genesis 42:11
1263.text: We are all of us sons of but one man. We are upright men. Your servants do not act as spies.”

1264.label: Genesis 42:12
1264.text: But he said to them: “Not so! Because YOU have come to see the exposed condition of the land!”

1265.label: Genesis 42:13
1265.text: At this they said: “Your servants are twelve brothers. We are the sons of but one man in the land of Caʹnaan; and here the youngest is with our father today, whereas the other one is no more.”

1266.label: Genesis 42:14
1266.text: However, Joseph said to them: “It is what I have spoken to YOU, saying, ‘YOU are spies!’

1267.label: Genesis 42:15
1267.text: By this YOU will be tested out. As Pharʹaoh lives, YOU will not go out of here except when YOUR youngest brother comes here.

1268.label: Genesis 42:16
1268.text: Send one of YOU that he may get YOUR brother while YOU have been bound, that YOUR words may be tested out as the truth in YOUR case. And if not, then, as Pharʹaoh lives, YOU are spies.”

1269.label: Genesis 42:17
1269.text: With that he put them together in custody for three days.

1270.label: Genesis 42:18
1270.text: After that Joseph said to them on the third day: “Do this and keep alive. I fear the [true] God.

1271.label: Genesis 42:19
1271.text: If YOU are upright, let one of YOUR brothers be kept bound in YOUR house of custody, but the rest of YOU go, take cereals for the famine in YOUR houses.

1272.label: Genesis 42:20
1272.text: Then YOU will bring YOUR youngest brother to me, that YOUR words may be found trustworthy; and YOU will not die.” And they proceeded to do so.

1273.label: Genesis 42:21
1273.text: And they began to say one to the other: “Unquestionably we are guilty with regard to our brother, because we saw the distress of his soul when he implored compassion on our part, but we did not listen. That is why this distress has come upon us.”

1274.label: Genesis 42:22
1274.text: Then Reuʹben answered them, saying: “Did not I say to YOU, ‘Do not sin against the child,’ but YOU did not listen? And now his blood, here it is certainly asked back.”

1275.label: Genesis 42:23
1275.text: As for them, they did not know that Joseph was listening, because there was an interpreter between them.

1276.label: Genesis 42:24
1276.text: Consequently he turned away from them and began to weep. Then he returned to them and spoke to them and took Simʹe·on from them and bound him before their eyes.

1277.label: Genesis 42:25
1277.text: After that Joseph gave the command, and they went filling up their receptacles with grain. Also, they were to return the money of the men to each one’s individual sack and to give them provisions for the journey. Accordingly it was done so to them.

1278.label: Genesis 42:26
1278.text: So they loaded their cereals upon their asses and got on their way from there.

1279.label: Genesis 42:27
1279.text: When one opened his sack to give fodder to his ass at the lodging place, he got to see his money, and here it was in the mouth of his bag.

1280.label: Genesis 42:28
1280.text: At that he said to his brothers: “My money has been returned and now here it is in my bag!” Then their hearts sank, so that they turned trembling to one another, saying: “What is this God has done to us?”

1281.label: Genesis 42:29
1281.text: At length they came to Jacob their father to the land of Caʹnaan and told him all the things that had befallen them, saying:

1282.label: Genesis 42:30
1282.text: “The man who is the lord of the country spoke harshly with us, since he took us for men spying on the country.

1283.label: Genesis 42:31
1283.text: But we said to him, ‘We are upright men. We do not act as spies.

1284.label: Genesis 42:32
1284.text: We are twelve brothers, the sons of our father. One is no more, and the youngest is today with our father in the land of Caʹnaan.’

1285.label: Genesis 42:33
1285.text: But the man who is the lord of the country said to us, ‘By this I am going to know YOU are upright: Have one brother of YOURS stay with me. Then YOU take something for the famine in YOUR houses and go.

1286.label: Genesis 42:34
1286.text: And bring YOUR youngest brother to me, that I may know that YOU are no spies but YOU are upright. Your brother I shall give back to YOU, and YOU may carry on business in the land.’”

1287.label: Genesis 42:35
1287.text: And it came about that when they were emptying their sacks here was each one’s bundle of money in his sack. And they as well as their father got to see their bundles of money, and they became afraid.

1288.label: Genesis 42:36
1288.text: Then Jacob their father exclaimed to them: “It is I YOU have bereaved! Joseph is no more and Simʹe·on is no more, and Benjamin YOU are going to take! It is upon me that all these things have come!”

1289.label: Genesis 42:37
1289.text: But Reuʹben said to his father: “My own two sons you may put to death if I do not bring him back to you. Give him over to my care, and I shall be the one to return him to you.”

1290.label: Genesis 42:38
1290.text: However, he said: “My son will not go down with YOU men, because his brother is dead and he has been left by himself. If a fatal accident should befall him on the way on which YOU would go, then YOU would certainly bring down my gray hairs with grief to Sheʹol.”

1291.label: Genesis 43:1
1291.text: And the famine was severe in the land.

1292.label: Genesis 43:2
1292.text: And it came about that as soon as they had finished eating up the cereals they had brought from Egypt, their father proceeded to say to them: “Return, buy a little food for us.”

1293.label: Genesis 43:3
1293.text: Then Judah said to him: “The man unmistakably bore witness to us, saying, ‘YOU must not see my face again unless YOUR brother is with YOU.’

1294.label: Genesis 43:4
1294.text: If you are sending our brother with us, we are willing to go down and buy food for you.

1295.label: Genesis 43:5
1295.text: But if you are not sending him, we shall not go down, because the man did say to us, ‘YOU must not see my face again unless YOUR brother is with YOU.’”

1296.label: Genesis 43:6
1296.text: And Israel exclaimed: “Why did YOU have to do harm to me by telling the man YOU had another brother?”

1297.label: Genesis 43:7
1297.text: At this they said: “The man directly inquired concerning us and our relatives, saying, ‘Is YOUR father yet alive? Do YOU have another brother?’ and we went on to tell him according to these facts. How could we know for certain that he would say, ‘Bring YOUR brother down’?”

1298.label: Genesis 43:8
1298.text: Finally Judah said to Israel his father: “Send the boy with me, that we may get up and go and that we may keep alive and not die off, both we and you and our little children.

1299.label: Genesis 43:9
1299.text: I shall be the one to be surety for him. Out of my hand you may exact the penalty for him. If I fail to bring him to you and present him to you, then I shall have sinned against you for all time.

1300.label: Genesis 43:10
1300.text: But if we had not lingered around, we should by now have been there and back these two times.”

1301.label: Genesis 43:11
1301.text: So Israel their father said to them: “If, then, that is the case, do this: Take the finest products of the land in YOUR receptacles and carry them down to the man as a gift: a little balsam, and a little honey, labdanum and resinous bark, pistachio nuts and almonds.

1302.label: Genesis 43:12
1302.text: Also, take double the money in YOUR hand; and the money that was returned in the mouth of YOUR bags YOU will take back in YOUR hand. Maybe it was a mistake.

1303.label: Genesis 43:13
1303.text: And take YOUR brother and get up, return to the man.

1304.label: Genesis 43:14
1304.text: And may God Almighty give YOU pity before the man, that he may certainly release to YOU YOUR other brother and Benjamin. But I, in case I must be bereaved, I shall certainly be bereaved!”

1305.label: Genesis 43:15
1305.text: Accordingly the men took this gift, and they took double the money in their hand and Benjamin. Then they rose and went their way down to Egypt and got to stand before Joseph.

1306.label: Genesis 43:16
1306.text: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he at once said to the man who was over his house: “Take the men to the house and slaughter animals and make preparation, because the men are to eat with me at noon.”

1307.label: Genesis 43:17
1307.text: Immediately the man did just as Joseph had said. So the man took the men to Joseph’s house.

1308.label: Genesis 43:18
1308.text: But the men got afraid because they had been taken to Joseph’s house, and they began to say: “It is because of the money that went back with us in our bags at the start that we are being brought here for them to fall upon us and attack us and to take us for slaves and also our asses!”

1309.label: Genesis 43:19
1309.text: Hence they approached the man who was over Joseph’s house and spoke to him at the entrance of the house,

1310.label: Genesis 43:20
1310.text: and they said: “Excuse us, my lord! We surely did come down at the start to buy food.

1311.label: Genesis 43:21
1311.text: But what occurred was that when we came to the lodging place and began opening our bags, why, here was the money of each one in the mouth of his bag, our money in full weight. So we would like to return it with our own hands.

1312.label: Genesis 43:22
1312.text: And more money we have brought down in our hands to buy food. We certainly do not know who placed our money in our bags.”

1313.label: Genesis 43:23
1313.text: Then he said: “It is all right with YOU. Do not be afraid. YOUR God and the God of YOUR father gave YOU treasure in YOUR bags. YOUR money came first to me.” After that he brought out Simʹe·on to them.

1314.label: Genesis 43:24
1314.text: Then the man brought the men into Joseph’s house and gave water that they might have their feet washed, and he gave fodder for their asses.

1315.label: Genesis 43:25
1315.text: And they proceeded to get the gift ready for Joseph’s coming at noon, because they had heard that it was there they were going to eat bread.

1316.label: Genesis 43:26
1316.text: When Joseph went on into the house, then they brought the gift that was in their hand to him into the house, and prostrated themselves to him to the earth.

1317.label: Genesis 43:27
1317.text: After this he inquired whether they were getting along well and said: “Is YOUR father, the aged man of whom YOU have spoken, getting along well? Is he still alive?”

1318.label: Genesis 43:28
1318.text: To this they said: “Your servant our father is getting along well. He is still alive.” Then they bowed down and prostrated themselves.

1319.label: Genesis 43:29
1319.text: When he raised his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother, the son of his mother, he went on to say: “Is this YOUR brother, the youngest one of whom YOU have spoken to me?” And he added: “May God show you his favor, my son.”

1320.label: Genesis 43:30
1320.text: Joseph was now in a hurry, because his inward emotions were excited toward his brother, so that he looked for a place to weep and he went into an interior room and gave way to tears there.

1321.label: Genesis 43:31
1321.text: After that he washed his face and went out and kept control of himself and said: “SET on the meal.”

1322.label: Genesis 43:32
1322.text: And they proceeded to set it on for him by himself and for them by themselves and for the Egyptians who were eating with him by themselves; for the Egyptians were not able to eat a meal with the Hebrews, because that is a detestable thing to the Egyptians.

1323.label: Genesis 43:33
1323.text: And they were seated before him, the firstborn according to his right as firstborn and the youngest according to his youngness; and the men kept looking at one another in amazement.

1324.label: Genesis 43:34
1324.text: And he kept having portions carried from before him to them, but he would increase Benjamin’s portion five times the size of the portions of all the others. So they continued banqueting and drinking with him to the full.

1325.label: Genesis 44:1
1325.text: Later on he commanded the man who was over his house, saying: “Fill the bags of the men with food to the extent they are able to carry it and place the money of each one in the mouth of his bag.

1326.label: Genesis 44:2
1326.text: But you must place my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the bag of the youngest and the money for his cereals.” So he did according to the word of Joseph which he had spoken.

1327.label: Genesis 44:3
1327.text: The morning had become light when the men were sent away, both they and their asses.

1328.label: Genesis 44:4
1328.text: They went out of the city. They had not gone far when Joseph said to the man who was over his house: “Get up! Chase after the men and be certain to overtake them and to say to them, ‘Why have YOU repaid bad for good?

1329.label: Genesis 44:5
1329.text: Is not this the thing that my master drinks from and by means of which he expertly reads omens? It is a bad deed YOU have committed.’”

1330.label: Genesis 44:6
1330.text: Eventually he overtook them and spoke these words to them.

1331.label: Genesis 44:7
